# Events

<!-- generated by `npm run schemas` from src/events — do not edit -->

Every event (stored, SSE, `/api/events`, webhook body) is the envelope below. `schemaVersion` is the
version of **that type's** payload schema; the JSON Schema for each is in `docs/schemas/<type>.v<N>.json`.
An additive (optional) field keeps the version; a removed, renamed or retyped field bumps it and adds
`<type>.v<N+1>.json` — the old file stays as documentation of what older consumers received.

Events stored before phase 3 read as v1 and are not re-validated.

Stored events are never rewritten. Superseded versions stay readable and documented: `job.prioritized.v1`, `decision.made.v1`, `jev.mode_changed.v1`, `job.prioritized.v2`, `decision.made.v2`, `router.mode_changed.v1`, `job.progressed.v1`, `question.escalated.v1`, `question.answered.v1`, `proposal.submitted.v1`, `proposal.escalated.v1`, `remote_access.changed.v1`
(phase 5 renamed Jev → router: `jev.mode_changed` became `router.mode_changed`; slice 2 made question
stages instance names: `question.escalated.target` and `question.answered.by` were `opus | fable | human` in v1;
issue #211 removed the router mode: `router.mode_changed` is retired, and v3 of `job.prioritized` and
`decision.made` carry no `mode` / `routerMode`).

```json
{ "schemaVersion": 1, "seq": 1, "id": "uuid", "type": "job.queued", "at": "ISO",
  "jobId": "…", "laneId": "…", "machineId": "…", "decisionId": "…", "questionId": "…", "data": { … } }
```

Schema: `docs/schemas/envelope.v1.json`. Payloads are strict: unknown keys are rejected.

Every `question.*` event names the **raising machine** — the machine the question was asked on — as the
`machineId` subject (and `laneId`, where the lane is known) and as `raisedBy` (`machineId`, `name`, `laneId`)
in its data: a snapshot taken when the question was asked, so it stays right after the job moves or the
machine is renamed or removed. Absent on a question asked before it was recorded, with nothing to fill it from.

## `job.queued`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/job.queued.v1.json`). A job was created from a source item; it waits at the queue gate until accepted (`job.accepted`).

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `spec` | object | yes |
| `priority` | number | yes |
| `source` | object | no |
| `forkOf` | object | no |
| `followOn` | object | no |

```json
{
  "spec": {
    "executor": "test",
    "payload": {
      "op": "echo"
    },
    "priority": 60,
    "goal": "g"
  },
  "priority": 60,
  "source": {
    "source": "github",
    "kind": "github",
    "key": "https://x/1",
    "number": 1
  }
}
```

## `job.prioritized`

Version 3 (`docs/schemas/job.prioritized.v3.json`). The router's advice arrived for a job; once per job, whatever its status then.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `advice` | object | yes |
| `statusAtAdvice` | `queued` \| `held` \| `claimed` \| `running` \| `waiting_answer` \| `operator_led` \| `parked` \| `waiting_on` \| `finished` \| `failed` \| `cancelled` \| `rejected` | yes |

```json
{
  "advice": {
    "action": "proceed_full",
    "reason": "ok",
    "details": {
      "intent": "x",
      "gatesAsked": true
    },
    "source": "fake",
    "at": "2026-10-02T00:00:00.000Z"
  },
  "statusAtAdvice": "queued"
}
```

## `job.held`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/job.held.v1.json`). A Decision held a job and its hold reason changed.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `reason` | string | yes |

```json
{
  "reason": "budget"
}
```

## `job.approved`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/job.approved.v1.json`). A human approved a job the router held (e.g. `ask_human`).

`data` is `{}`.

```json
{}
```

## `job.claimed`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/job.claimed.v1.json`). A Decision assigned a job to a lane.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `attempts` | integer | yes |
| `effectivePriority` | number | yes |
| `reason` | string | yes |

```json
{
  "attempts": 1,
  "effectivePriority": 50,
  "reason": "idle lane"
}
```

## `job.started`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/job.started.v1.json`). The executor began running a claimed job.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `attempts` | integer | yes |

```json
{
  "attempts": 1
}
```

## `job.progressed`

Version 2 (`docs/schemas/job.progressed.v2.json`). An executor reported progress: a progress message, the job's task count (done of total), or both; at most one per job per 500 ms.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `message` | string | no |
| `tasks` | object | no |

```json
{
  "message": "Running the checks",
  "tasks": {
    "done": 2,
    "total": 5
  }
}
```

## `job.finished`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/job.finished.v1.json`). A job ended successfully. `partlyDone` (issue #579): it ended partly done — the URL of its own pull request that ships part of its item ("Part of #N"); the next part runs once that is merged.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `result` | any | yes |
| `partlyDone` | string | no |

```json
{
  "result": {
    "ok": true
  }
}
```

## `job.failed`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/job.failed.v1.json`). A job ended with an error. `priority`, `high` (issue #535): the job's live priority, and whether it is at or above the high-priority threshold. `tldr` (issue #569): for a long question, what a notification leads with — its TL;DR when written, else the agent's own summary; absent for a short one or with the TL;DR off.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `error` | string | yes |
| `priority` | number | no |
| `high` | boolean | no |

```json
{
  "error": "boom"
}
```

## `job.cancelled`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/job.cancelled.v1.json`). A job was cancelled. `reason`: why, as the hopper or its source names it (`cancelled in UI` for a person's cancel). `note` (issue #1460): the person's own words why, when they gave some; never told to the source.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `reason` | string | yes |
| `note` | string | no |

```json
{
  "reason": "cancelled while queued"
}
```

## `job.requeued`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/job.requeued.v1.json`). A job went back to the queue (restart recovery, a question answered or closed, or its machine out of reach of the hopper at its start). `reason` is a free string.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `from` | string | yes |
| `reason` | string | yes |

```json
{
  "from": "waiting_answer",
  "reason": "answered"
}
```

## `job.reattached`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/job.reattached.v1.json`). The executor watches a job's live external work again (the herdr pane and Claude) without sending anything. `reason` `daemon restart`: restart recovery kept a running job running on its lane. `reason` `answered in the pane`: the owner typed the answer into a waiting job's pane; the job runs again on a lane. `reason` `link restored` (issue #752): the machine's link is back after `job.link_lost` and the job's pane is alive; it goes on from its saved turn. `reason` `its hopper stopped` (issue #1662): another hopper on the same database took over a running job whose lease ended.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `reason` | string | yes |

```json
{
  "reason": "daemon restart"
}
```

## `job.link_lost`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/job.link_lost.v1.json`). The link to the running job's machine (`machine`) dropped while it was watched (issue #752). The job is held: it stays `running` on its lane, and the hopper asks every second whether its pane is alive again. `since`: when the link was found down. `failsAt`: when the job fails if the link is not back (the link grace). It goes on with `job.reattached` (reason `link restored`), or fails with "machine <id> did not reconnect within <n> s" and its cleanup deferred.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `machine` | string | yes |
| `since` | string | yes |
| `failsAt` | string | yes |

```json
{
  "machine": "lab",
  "since": "2026-10-10T12:00:00.000Z",
  "failsAt": "2026-10-10T12:02:00.000Z"
}
```

## `job.reprioritized`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/job.reprioritized.v1.json`). A source re-sorted a waiting job.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `from` | number | yes |
| `to` | number | yes |
| `reason` | string | yes |

```json
{
  "from": 50,
  "to": 80,
  "reason": "project:Priority=P1"
}
```

## `job.respecified`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/job.respecified.v1.json`). A sync worked out a job that has not started from the config as it is now (issue #375), and its executor, model, work tree, default work tree, machine pin or routing rule changed. `from` and `to` are what the source and routing rules gave it; a part changed on the job by hand keeps the hand value, so the spec can differ from `to`.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `from` | object | yes |
| `to` | object | yes |

```json
{
  "from": {
    "executor": "herdr-claude",
    "cwd": "~/code/app"
  },
  "to": {
    "executor": "herdr-claude",
    "model": "claude-opus-5-5",
    "cwd": "~/code/app-gpu",
    "machineId": "gpu",
    "rule": "gpu"
  }
}
```

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/lane.opened.v1.json`). A Decision opened a lane.

`data` is `{}`.

```json
{}
```

## `lane.closed`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/lane.closed.v1.json`). A lane closed (decision reason, `drained`, or `daemon restart`).

## `lane.unhealthy`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/lane.unhealthy.v1.json`). A lane is unhealthy (issue #2234): its last `failures` starts failed with the same start error, `error` the last; it takes no new job until `until`.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `failures` | integer | yes |
| `error` | string | yes |
| `since` | string | yes |
| `until` | string | yes |

```json
{
  "failures": 3,
  "error": "claude did not start in 3 attempts: pane w1:p3 never set up the job's container runtime within 60000 ms",
  "since": "2026-10-20T13:10:00.000Z",
  "until": "2026-10-20T13:52:00.000Z"
}
```

## `decision.made`

Version 3 (`docs/schemas/decision.made.v3.json`). The engine recorded a Decision.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `decisionId` | string | yes |
| `trigger` | string | yes |
| `starts` | object[] | yes |
| `holds` | object[] | yes |
| `lanes` | object[] | yes |
| `divergences` | object[] | yes |
| `waits` | object[] | no |

```json
{
  "decisionId": "d1",
  "trigger": "tick",
  "starts": [
    {
      "jobId": "j1",
      "laneId": "m/lane-1",
      "machineId": "m",
      "effectivePriority": 50,
      "reason": "idle lane"
    }
  ],
  "holds": [
    {
      "jobId": "j2",
      "reason": "full"
    }
  ],
  "waits": [
    {
      "jobId": "j3",
      "reason": "waiting for a lane: machine local's lane cap is 4, all 4 in use"
    }
  ],
  "lanes": [
    {
      "machineId": "m",
      "current": 0,
      "target": 1,
      "open": 1,
      "close": [],
      "drain": [],
      "reason": "work waiting"
    }
  ],
  "divergences": [
    {
      "jobId": "j1",
      "advice": "ask_human",
      "native": "start",
      "withAdvice": "hold",
      "note": "n"
    }
  ]
}
```

## `question.asked`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/question.asked.v1.json`). A running job paused on a question. `priority`, `high` (issue #535): the job's live priority, and whether it is at or above the high-priority threshold. `text`: the question as the agent wrote it, Markdown source (issue #569).

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `questionId` | string | yes |
| `text` | string | yes |
| `detectedBy` | string | yes |
| `raisedBy` | object | no |
| `priority` | number | no |
| `high` | boolean | no |

```json
{
  "questionId": "q1",
  "text": "which?",
  "detectedBy": "marker",
  "raisedBy": {
    "machineId": "desk",
    "name": "Desk tower",
    "laneId": "desk/lane-1"
  }
}
```

## `question.escalated`

Version 2 (`docs/schemas/question.escalated.v2.json`). A question entered a stage — `target` is an escalation level's instance name, or `human` — or the human was re-notified. `reason` says why it climbed: the reply or the failure of the level below, or a risk rule hit. `priority`, `high` (issue #535): the job's live priority, and whether it is at or above the high-priority threshold. `holds` (issue #679): every hold on the level's answer that sent it, strongest first — `guard` (`by` `risk` or `guard`, the `guards` by name), `high_priority`, `auto_answer_off`, `low_confidence` (with the `confidence` and the `threshold`). A risk hold the Decider made (issue #679) carries `decider` in place of `guards`: its `risk`, `categories`, `confidence` and `threshold`, or the `error` it failed with.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `questionId` | string | yes |
| `target` | string | yes |
| `reason` | string | yes |
| `text` | string | yes |
| `jobId` | string | yes |
| `goal` | string | no |
| `answerUrl` | string | no |
| `notifyCount` | integer | no |
| `renotify` | boolean | no |
| `lapsesAt` | string | no |
| `tldr` | string | no |
| `raisedBy` | object | no |
| `priority` | number | no |
| `high` | boolean | no |

```json
{
  "questionId": "q1",
  "target": "human",
  "reason": "asked",
  "text": "which?",
  "jobId": "j1",
  "goal": "g",
  "answerUrl": "http://127.0.0.1/q",
  "notifyCount": 0,
  "renotify": true
}
```

## `question.escalated_to_human`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/question.escalated_to_human.v1.json`). A question reached the human stage: every level escalated, there are no levels, or a risk rule hit. Once per question, right after its `question.escalated` with `target` `human`; never on a level hop or a re-notification. Subscribe to it to hear only the questions the owner must answer: the Grok Bot routine webhook listens to it and to no `question.escalated` (issue #481). `priority`, `high` (issue #535): the job's live priority, and whether it is at or above the high-priority threshold. `holds` (issue #679): every hold on the level's answer that sent it, strongest first — `guard` (`by` `risk` or `guard`, the `guards` by name), `high_priority`, `auto_answer_off`, `low_confidence` (with the `confidence` and the `threshold`). A risk hold the Decider made (issue #679) carries `decider` in place of `guards`: its `risk`, `categories`, `confidence` and `threshold`, or the `error` it failed with.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `questionId` | string | yes |
| `reason` | string | yes |
| `text` | string | yes |
| `jobId` | string | yes |
| `goal` | string | no |
| `answerUrl` | string | yes |
| `notifyCount` | integer | yes |
| `lapsesAt` | string | no |
| `tldr` | string | no |
| `raisedBy` | object | no |
| `priority` | number | no |
| `high` | boolean | no |
| `holds` | object[] | no |

```json
{
  "questionId": "q1",
  "reason": "fable: the owner's call",
  "text": "which?",
  "jobId": "j1",
  "goal": "g",
  "answerUrl": "http://127.0.0.1/q",
  "notifyCount": 1,
  "raisedBy": {
    "machineId": "desk",
    "name": "Desk tower",
    "laneId": "desk/lane-1"
  },
  "priority": 75,
  "high": true,
  "holds": [
    {
      "reason": "guard",
      "by": "risk",
      "guards": [
        "credentials"
      ]
    },
    {
      "reason": "low_confidence",
      "confidence": "medium",
      "threshold": "high"
    }
  ]
}
```

## `question.answered`

Version 2 (`docs/schemas/question.answered.v2.json`). An answer was accepted: an escalation level's (`by` = the level instance; `auto: true` with its `confidence`: it went into the job with no person, issue #632), or the human's (`via: "pane"` when they typed it into the job's pane: the job already runs again, nothing is typed for them).

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `questionId` | string | yes |
| `by` | string | yes |
| `answer` | string | yes |
| `via` | string | no |
| `auto` | boolean | no |
| `confidence` | `low` \| `medium` \| `high` | no |
| `raisedBy` | object | no |

```json
{
  "questionId": "q1",
  "by": "human",
  "answer": "yes"
}
```

## `question.closed`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/question.closed.v1.json`). The owner closed an open question without answering (UI Close). The job resumes with `answer`, the fixed close text, typed in; any escalation level call in flight is aborted.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `questionId` | string | yes |
| `answer` | string | yes |
| `raisedBy` | object | no |

```json
{
  "questionId": "q1",
  "answer": "The owner closed this question without answering. Continue on your own judgement; if you cannot, end with HOPPER_FAILED and say why."
}
```

## `question.dismissed`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/question.dismissed.v1.json`). The owner dismissed an open question (UI Dismiss): it needs no action any more. Nothing is typed into the job; a job still waiting on it is cancelled (`job.cancelled`, reason `question dismissed`); any escalation level call in flight is aborted.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `questionId` | string | yes |
| `raisedBy` | object | no |

```json
{
  "questionId": "q1"
}
```

## `question.expired`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/question.expired.v1.json`). The human stage timed out and the job fails.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `questionId` | string | yes |
| `after_ms` | number | yes |
| `raisedBy` | object | no |

```json
{
  "questionId": "q1",
  "after_ms": 1000
}
```

## `question.lapsed`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/question.lapsed.v1.json`). Nobody answered a dialog in time: the agent denied it by itself when its countdown ran out (Claude Code's auto-deny), and the job went on (`job.reattached`, reason `the dialog lapsed`). `lapsesAt` is when the countdown ended. Not an answer: nothing is typed, and no stage answered; any escalation level call in flight is aborted.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `questionId` | string | yes |
| `lapsesAt` | string | yes |
| `raisedBy` | object | no |

```json
{
  "questionId": "q1",
  "lapsesAt": "2026-10-07T21:43:59.000Z"
}
```

## `question.cancelled`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/question.cancelled.v1.json`). An open question was cancelled: its job ended or is gone (at a restart, or on the sweep), so nothing waits on it any more. Nothing is typed into the job; any escalation level call in flight is aborted. The UI drops it from the open questions and the Needs you count (issue #1457).

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `questionId` | string | yes |
| `raisedBy` | object | no |

```json
{
  "questionId": "q1"
}
```

## `update.available`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/update.available.v1.json`). A check found a newer target on the update channel than the installed commit (once per target). `ref` is the branch of the channel; `changes` counts its commits not installed (an operator detail; the UI shows the bullets of WHATS-NEW.md instead). `pullRequest` (issue #652): the number of the pull request the target is the merge of, whose checks passed; only such a target is announced, a held one never.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `from` | string | yes |
| `to` | string | yes |
| `ref` | string | yes |
| `changes` | integer | yes |
| `pullRequest` | integer | no |

```json
{
  "from": "a1b2c3d",
  "to": "e4f5a6b",
  "ref": "stable",
  "changes": 3,
  "pullRequest": 775
}
```

## `update.started`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/update.started.v1.json`). Applying an update began (UI, or auto-update): the target is built beside the running install. Running jobs keep running.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `from` | string | yes |
| `to` | string | yes |
| `ref` | string | yes |

```json
{
  "from": "a1b2c3d",
  "to": "e4f5a6b",
  "ref": "stable"
}
```

## `update.applied`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/update.applied.v1.json`). The first boot on an applied update: the install now runs `to`. Recovery reattached what was running.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `from` | string | yes |
| `to` | string | yes |
| `ref` | string | yes |

```json
{
  "from": "a1b2c3d",
  "to": "e4f5a6b",
  "ref": "stable"
}
```

## `update.failed`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/update.failed.v1.json`). Applying an update failed (fetch, build, the new build not loading, or the swap) and the install is unchanged — or a boot after an update is not on the applied commit.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `to` | string | yes |
| `error` | string | yes |

```json
{
  "to": "e4f5a6b",
  "error": "the new build does not load: SyntaxError"
}
```

## `plugin.installed`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/plugin.installed.v1.json`). A plugin was installed from the plugin store into the plugin dir (UI Install or Update), at the store's commit `commit`. A plugin new to this process is loaded at once; one installed again runs its new code after a restart.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | string | yes |
| `role` | `router` \| `queue-sorter` \| `escalation-level` \| `executor` \| `job-source` \| `machine-source` \| `usage-source` \| `notifier` \| `vault-backend` | yes |
| `commit` | string | yes |

```json
{
  "id": "echo-executor",
  "role": "executor",
  "commit": "e4f5a6b"
}
```

## `plugin.removed`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/plugin.removed.v1.json`). A store install was removed from the plugin dir (UI Remove). Nothing in the plugins config named it.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | string | yes |

```json
{
  "id": "echo-executor"
}
```

## `job.accepted`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/job.accepted.v1.json`). A job passed the queue gate and may run: `by` `pre-sort` (the gate auto-accepts, or the user took the pre-sort with Accept pre-sort), or `user` (moved into the user order).

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `by` | `user` \| `pre-sort` | yes |

```json
{
  "by": "pre-sort"
}
```

## `job.rejected`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/job.rejected.v1.json`). A waiting job was turned away at the queue gate: it ends `rejected`, is kept, and never runs. `by` `user` (UI Reject, with the reason the user gave, else `rejected by the user`) or `pre-sort` (the queue sorter rejected it); `reason` is also the job's `error`. Its source is told; on GitHub the issue is left as it is — no label, no comment, never closed — and is not taken again until it is assigned to the account again or run again (issue #387).

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `by` | `user` \| `pre-sort` | yes |
| `reason` | string | yes |

```json
{
  "by": "user",
  "reason": "rejected by the user"
}
```

## `queue.ordered`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/queue.ordered.v1.json`). The user ordered the queue: `jobIds`, first to last, run before every job not in it.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `jobIds` | string[] | yes |

```json
{
  "jobIds": [
    "j2",
    "j1"
  ]
}
```

## `queue.gate_changed`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/queue.gate_changed.v1.json`). The queue gate was changed: its mode (`auto-accept` or `review`) or its throttle (`autoAcceptPerHour`, null for none).

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `from` | object | yes |
| `to` | object | yes |

```json
{
  "from": {
    "mode": "auto-accept",
    "autoAcceptPerHour": null
  },
```

## `job.claimed_by_operator`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/job.claimed_by_operator.v1.json`). An operator claimed the waiting job as operator-led (issue #318): the work is done by hand — at a terminal, or in an IDE the hopper has no pane in — not by an executor. The job holds no lane and is never run; it is finished when its closing pull request reaches the completion, as any job is, and cancelled as any job is.

`data` is `{}`.

```json
{}
```

## `job.rerun`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/job.rerun.v1.json`). The user (`by: "user"`), or the failure assessor (`by: "assessor"`: a retry, a redirect, a held job released — issue #509), or the hopper's tending of a waiting pull request (`by: "tending"`: merge conflicts or failing checks, issue #736; `job.pull_request_tended` follows), or the item reconciler (`by: "reconciler"`: its pull request closed without a merge on GitHub, the first time in a row, issue #1891), asked for an ended job's item to run again (UI Run again, a re-run): its source gave the item back (on GitHub: a closed issue reopened, the end labels gone) and the new job was queued in the same step, its `job.queued` just before this event and its `rerunOf` this job. The ended job is kept as it ended; a failed one is no longer a locked entry. A person's run again from Failures — a failure's Retry, a hand-off's I fixed it, or Continue in a new job — names who: `person`, and the way, `via` `ui` or `cli` (issue #623).

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `by` | `user` \| `assessor` \| `tending` \| `reconciler` | yes |
| `person` | string | no |
| `via` | `ui` \| `cli` \| `api` | no |

```json
{
  "by": "user"
}
```

## `job.rework_requested`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/job.rework_requested.v1.json`). A person sent a finished job's open pull request back for rework (issue #724: the card in Pull requests, `hopper job rework`, or `POST /ui/api/jobs/:id/rework`), with notes: the pull request became a draft and stays open on its branch, the job no longer follows it, and the new job of its item (`nextJobId`, its `rerunOf` this job) reworks it, told the notes. That job is done only when it pushed to the pull request after the rework and marked it ready. `person` and `via` (`ui`, `cli`): who acted and the way.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `pullRequest` | string | yes |
| `notes` | string | yes |
| `nextJobId` | string | yes |
| `person` | string | no |
| `via` | `ui` \| `cli` \| `api` | no |

```json
{
  "pullRequest": "https://github.com/owner/repo/pull/14",
  "notes": "Rename the flag.",
  "nextJobId": "j-2",
  "person": "operator",
  "via": "ui"
}
```

## `job.dismissed`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/job.dismissed.v1.json`). A locked entry was dismissed (issue #355): the failed job stays failed and leaves the queue. It can still be run again. Its issue keeps `hopper:failed`. `by`: `user` (a person), or, by itself, nothing waits on it any more (issue #1123): `superseded` (a newer job of its item took its place) or `item_closed` (its item is closed at its source, done or dropped). Only a person's dismissal opens a hand-off.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `by` | `user` \| `superseded` \| `item_closed` | yes |

```json
{
  "by": "user"
}
```

## `job.unassigned`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/job.unassigned.v1.json`). A started job's issue is no longer assigned to `assignee`, the account it was taken for (issue #387). The job runs on, flagged (`sourceState.sync.unassignedAt`); the user decides whether to stop it. A waiting job is cancelled `unassigned` instead. Recorded once per flag.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `assignee` | string | yes |

```json
{
  "assignee": "octocat"
}
```

## `job.reassigned`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/job.reassigned.v1.json`). A flagged job's issue is assigned to `assignee` again (issue #387): the flag is cleared.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `assignee` | string | yes |

```json
{
  "assignee": "octocat"
}
```

## `job.work_kept`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/job.work_kept.v1.json`). The reap at the job's end (issue #401), or a later sweep (issue #410), kept its scratch dir and its job worktrees (issue #1188: in its work tree's `.worktrees`): each of `paths` is a repository there holding uncommitted or unpushed work. Nothing in it was removed; the job's processes were still stopped. The sweep tries again on each pass, and removes it once the work is pushed (`job.work_removed`).

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `paths` | string[] | yes |

```json
{
  "paths": [
    "/home/me/hopper-jobs/.worktrees/hopper/7d0c9b1e-2f4a-4c55-9e3b-1a2b3c4d5e6f"
  ]
}
```

## `job.work_removed`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/job.work_removed.v1.json`). The sweep (issue #410), or the job's next reap, removed the scratch dir a reap had kept (`job.work_kept`): its work is now committed and pushed. `paths` is the scratch dir removed. With `discarded` (issue #1010), a person discarded the kept work in Failures, Work not pushed: the scratch dir was removed whatever it held; `person` and `via` say who and the way. With `discarded` and `reason` (issue #1187), the sweep discarded it with no person, as nobody waits on it: `merged` (its item is done, issue #1105), `superseded` (a newer job of its item finished with nothing kept), `proposal` or `research` (it finished a proposal or a research report, never work to push), `pushed` (issue #2087: the hopper pushed each commit of it for the job). With `gone` (issue #1120), the sweep found the scratch dir and its job worktree no longer on the job's machine (removed by hand, or by a cleanup outside the hopper): the record is resolved, and nothing was removed.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `paths` | string[] | yes |
| `discarded` | boolean | no |
| `gone` | boolean | no |
| `reason` | `merged` \| `superseded` \| `proposal` \| `research` \| `pushed` | no |
| `person` | string | no |
| `via` | `ui` \| `cli` \| `api` | no |

```json
{
  "paths": [
    "/home/me/hopper-jobs/.worktrees/@scratch/7d0c9b1e-2f4a-4c55-9e3b-1a2b3c4d5e6f"
  ]
}
```

## `job.work_discard_failed`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/job.work_discard_failed.v1.json`). A person discarded the kept work in Failures, Work not pushed (issue #1010), and the removal on the job's machine, which runs after the answer (issue #1194), failed: `error` says why (its machine out of reach, or a client older than the discard that kept it). The work is still kept, and Discard is offered again. `person` and `via` say who and the way.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `error` | string | yes |
| `person` | string | no |
| `via` | `ui` \| `cli` \| `api` | no |

```json
{
  "error": "job 7d0c9b1e's work cannot be discarded: its machine desk is out of reach",
  "person": "Pat",
  "via": "ui"
}
```

## `job.give_back_failed`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/job.give_back_failed.v1.json`). A person's act on this ended job that gives its item back was answered at once — Run again (`act` `rerun`), Rework (`rework`), Failures' Retry (`retry`), a hand-off's Continue (`continue`) or I fixed it (`fixed`), Push it (`push`), Tend again (`tend`) —, and its source's give-back, which runs after the answer (issue #1194) — on GitHub the issue reopened, assigned and its end labels gone, for Rework the pull request made a draft first —, or what follows it, failed: `error` says why (GitHub out of reach or refusing, the issue no longer assigned to the connected account, a newer job of its item made meanwhile, for Retry its work done at its source). No new job was made, and the act is offered again. Through a GitHub outbox each act is a row (issue #1238 parts 4 and 5): for Run again and Rework GitHub refusing for now is tried again after a backoff; the other acts are checked again at the send, and a run that fails fails the row at once. This is recorded once the row failed for good. `person` and `via` say who and the way.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `act` | `rerun` \| `rework` \| `retry` \| `continue` \| `fixed` \| `push` \| `tend` | yes |
| `error` | string | yes |
| `person` | string | no |
| `via` | `ui` \| `cli` \| `api` | no |

```json
{
  "act": "rerun",
  "error": "its source could not give the item back: GitHub answered 502",
  "person": "Pat",
  "via": "ui"
}
```

## `job.pull_request_act_failed`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/job.pull_request_act_failed.v1.json`). A person's Merge now (`act` `merge`) or Close PR (`close`) on this finished job's open pull request was answered at once (issue #1194), and its source's merge or close, which runs after the answer, failed for good: `error` says why (GitHub refused it — a draft, merge conflicts, a required check —, or was out of reach at each of the GitHub outbox's attempts, issue #1238, or the pull request was no longer open). Recorded once, when its outbox row fails. The pull request stays as it was, and the act is offered again. `person` and `via` say who and the way.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `act` | `merge` \| `close` | yes |
| `error` | string | yes |
| `person` | string | no |
| `via` | `ui` \| `cli` \| `api` | no |

```json
{
  "act": "merge",
  "error": "merge refused: Pull Request is not mergeable (HTTP 405)",
  "person": "Pat",
  "via": "ui"
}
```

## `job.containers_removed`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/job.containers_removed.v1.json`). The job's reap (issue #1120), at its end or in a later sweep, removed the containers and volumes on its machine labelled with its id (`hopper.job=<job id>`): `containers`, each with its anonymous volumes, and `volumes`, by name. The sweep reaps an ended job that still has one, whatever its age. A timed-out job's reap removes none: it may go on there. `details` (issue #975): what the reap said of each container before it removed it — its `name`, `image`, and when it started (`startedAt`) and stopped (`stoppedAt`), each absent when it never did —, which the job's parts list shows; absent from a client older than this.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `containers` | string[] | yes |
| `volumes` | string[] | yes |
| `details` | object[] | no |

```json
{
  "containers": [
    "3f2a9c1b7d4e"
  ],
  "volumes": [
    "hopper-test-db"
  ],
  "details": [
    {
      "id": "3f2a9c1b7d4e",
      "name": "hopper-test-db",
      "image": "docker.io/library/postgres:16",
      "startedAt": "2026-10-08T00:02:00.000Z",
      "stoppedAt": "2026-10-08T00:09:00.000Z"
    }
  ]
}
```

## `job.cleanup_deferred`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/job.cleanup_deferred.v1.json`). The job ended, but its cleanup could not reach its machine (`error`), so its pane and agent may still run there. Recorded once per deferral; the cleanup is tried again on every tick, and a waiting job of the same item is held until it goes through.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `error` | string | yes |

```json
{
  "error": "herdr: client is not dialled in"
}
```

## `job.cleaned_up`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/job.cleaned_up.v1.json`). A deferred cleanup went through: the job's pane is closed and its work reaped. `deferredAt` is when it was deferred. `by: "user"`: the user marked it cleaned up (they closed the pane by hand, or its machine is gone for good), and it is no longer tried. `dueAt` (issue #1570): a stop of the hopper came between the job's end and its cleanup, which the next start did from its record; `dueAt` is when the record was written, at the job's end. Recorded only for a deferred cleanup, or one done after a stop.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `deferredAt` | string | no |
| `dueAt` | string | no |
| `by` | `user` | no |

```json
{
  "deferredAt": "2026-10-07T21:31:00.000Z"
}
```

## `job.pod_removed`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/job.pod_removed.v1.json`). The sweep (issue #1570), at startup and then every 10 minutes, deleted the job's pod and removed its machine: the job ended, no cleanup was still owed, and its pod was still there with this hopper's instance label (a delete that failed, or a hopper older than the cleanup record). `executor` is the executor that started it.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `executor` | string | yes |

```json
{
  "executor": "kubernetes"
}
```

## `job.parked`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/job.parked.v1.json`). A person, auto-park (issues #650, #2335: `auto`, its question waited on a person a few seconds, or its proposal or research report reached the human stage; `why` says so), or the busy-machine move (issue #1977: `auto`, a job queued to resume on a full machine while another had room; `why` says so) parked a running job or one on a question, a proposal or a research report (issue #501): its lane is free, its pane and agent ended, and its work tree, branch, agent session and open question are kept. `machineId`: the machine it returns to when re-queued. `by`, `via`, `reason` (issue #2167): the person who parked it, the way they did (`ui`, `cli`, `api`), and the reason they gave; a running job that parked it through the `park` skill (`POST /job/park`) is `by` `job <its id>`, `via` `job`. A parked job never runs, its question never expires, and its proposal or research report is neither reviewed nor decided, until it is re-queued or cancelled.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `from` | `running` \| `waiting_answer` | yes |
| `machineId` | string | no |
| `auto` | boolean | no |
| `why` | string | no |
| `by` | string | no |
| `via` | `ui` \| `cli` \| `api` \| `job` | no |
| `reason` | string | no |

```json
{
  "from": "waiting_answer",
  "machineId": "laptop",
  "auto": true,
  "why": "Parked automatically: the question waited 30 min."
}
```

## `job.unparked`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/job.unparked.v1.json`). A person, or the signed-out move (issue #1211), re-queued a parked job (issue #501). `to` `queued`: it waits, pinned to its machine, and its claim resumes its agent session there (`claude --resume`), with the answer kept while it was parked, if any. `to` `waiting_answer`: its question is still open; the answer resumes it, and the human timeout starts again. `by`, `via` (issue #2167): the person who picked it up and the way (`ui`, `cli`, `api`), or `job <its id>` and `job` for a running job that picked up a proposal or research report it parked through the `park` skill. `elsewhere` (issue #921): picked up to resume on another machine from its checkpoint: it is not pinned to its machine, and its claim rebuilds its work tree from the checkpoint on the machine it gets and resumes its agent session there. The signed-out move and the busy-machine move (issue #1977) re-queue with `elsewhere` too: from the checkpoint, or as a new start when the agent never got its task.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `to` | `queued` \| `waiting_answer` | yes |
| `elsewhere` | boolean | no |
| `by` | string | no |
| `via` | `ui` \| `cli` \| `api` \| `job` | no |

```json
{
  "to": "queued",
  "elsewhere": true
}
```

## `job.continued`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/job.continued.v1.json`). An ended job goes on in its own agent session: the job is queued again, pinned to the machine it ran on, and its claim resumes that session in its work tree (`claude --resume`). A person resolved its hand-off with Continue (issue #551), told the failure and the person's note: `handoffId`, the hand-off it resolved. Or the failure assessor continued a timed-out job still at work (issue #630), told it timed out while at work: `recordId`, its failure record. Or a person chose Push it on its work not pushed (issue #1010) — a failed, finished or cancelled job —, told to push the work its work tree kept and open the pull request: `keptWork`. Or the failure sweep did so by itself for a finished job (issue #1472, Push it by itself, the failures setting `auto.push`): `keptWork` and `auto`.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `handoffId` | string | no |
| `recordId` | string | no |
| `keptWork` | boolean | no |
| `auto` | boolean | no |

```json
{
  "handoffId": "h1"
}
```

## `job.waiting`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/job.waiting.v1.json`). The job waits on something it named (issue #483): it ended its turn with HOPPER_WAITING. `for`: what it waits for; `until`: how it will know, as it wrote it; `on` (issue #1245): what it waits on, typed — a pull request (`number`, `about`: `checks`, `merge` or `review`), a job, an item, a person's question, a `sandbox` or `template` approval, a vault grant, its own command, or an outside event —, from its `on:` line, else read from what it wrote; absent only on a wait from before; `ownCommand` (issue #1037): `until` names its own background command, so it shows as running. Its status is `waiting_on`: no question opens, its lane is free, its pane and agent stay on its machine, and nothing is typed into it. It goes on when its agent goes on by itself (`job.reattached`, reason `the wait ended in the pane`) or a person ends the wait (`job.wait_ended`), or the hopper ends it with an answer the job asked it for (issue #998), or when the event that settles what it waits on comes (issue #1245): the pull request merged or closed, the job ended, the item's issue closed, the question answered, closed, dismissed or expired, its vault grant given or denied.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `for` | string | yes |
| `until` | string | no |
| `on` | any | no |
| `ownCommand` | boolean | no |

```json
{
  "for": "write access to the repository",
  "until": "a background poll of the push",
  "on": {
    "kind": "outside",
    "what": "write access to the repository"
  }
}
```

## `job.wait_ended`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/job.wait_ended.v1.json`). A person ended a job's own wait (issue #483), or the hopper did (`by: hopper`, issue #998) when an answer the job asked it for is ready (a skill request: a sandbox, a template, a credential): the job is queued again, pinned to its machine, and its claim tells it in its pane that the thing it waits for has happened, with the person's `note`, or the hopper's answer, if any. `check` (issue #1694): the hopper's wait check ended it — its condition, as a key (`items_ended:…`, `job_ended:<id>`, `question_settled:<id>`, `command_exited`) —; a later wait of the job on the same items is not woken for them again. `comment` (issue #2159): the link of the comment that woke it — a trusted account (the user's connected account or a maintainer of the repository) commented on the job's issue or its own pull request while it waited; the job is told the comment as untrusted text.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `by` | `person` \| `hopper` | yes |
| `note` | string | no |
| `check` | string | no |
| `comment` | string | no |

```json
{
  "by": "person",
  "note": "Write access is granted."
}
```

## `job.own_command_nudged`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/job.own_command_nudged.v1.json`). A job waiting on its own background command (issue #1037, `ownCommand` on its wait): its pane showed no background work for the grace (`HOPPER_OWN_COMMAND_GRACE_MS`) and its agent did not go on, so the hopper typed one nudge into its pane: check the command, then go on. `delivered`: false when its pane or agent was gone. Once per wait.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `delivered` | boolean | yes |

```json
{
  "delivered": true
}
```

## `job.own_command_stuck`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/job.own_command_stuck.v1.json`). A job waiting on its own background command (issue #1037) did not go on within the grace after its nudge: its wait was flagged stuck (`stuckAt`). Before issue #1694 only; now its wait check ends such a wait.

`data` is `{}`.

```json
{}
```

## `job.wait_polled`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/job.wait_polled.v1.json`). A job waiting on its own background command (issue #1037) asks the hopper the same read again and again (issue #1210): its command polls hopper state, a pull request or an issue. `on`: what it polls, now its wait's `on`, so the UI and the ledger say what it waits on. It stays its own command, so it holds no tending queue. The hopper ends the wait (`job.wait_ended`, by the hopper) an hour after it began, on its next poll, with the last answer. Once per wait.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `on` | any | yes |

```json
{
  "on": {
    "kind": "pull_request",
    "repo": "octo/tools",
    "number": 8,
    "about": "merge"
  }
}
```

## `job.waited_pull_request_ended`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/job.waited_pull_request_ended.v1.json`). A pull request a job waits on (issue #1433), which no follow of a job recorded the end of, was seen merged or closed without a merge at a sync of the job's source: the source reads each pull request a job's own wait names. Recorded on each job waiting on it; the hopper wakes them (`job.wait_ended { by: hopper }`), as `job.pull_request_merged` or `job.pull_request_closed` would. `pullRequest`: its URL; `state`: `merged` or `closed`.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `pullRequest` | string | yes |
| `state` | `merged` \| `closed` | yes |

```json
{
  "pullRequest": "https://github.com/octo/tools/pull/8",
  "state": "closed"
}
```

## `job.waited_items_ended`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/job.waited_items_ended.v1.json`). Every item a job's own wait names (issue #1508) ended, as a sync of the job's source read them: an issue closed, a pull request merged or closed, a workflow run completed. The wait is on an item, or on an outside event whose text names issues, pull requests (`owner/name#N`, `name#N` of the job's owner, `issue N`, a link) or workflow runs (`<repo> run N`, `workflow run N`, a link). They may have ended before the wait began. Also at once when one of them does not exist, or the hopper cannot read it (issues #1691, #2066): then `items` holds only those, `state` `not_found`, so the job rewrites its wait. The hopper wakes the job (`job.wait_ended { by: hopper }`). Once per wait; a job woken so that waits again on the same items is not woken for them again until the hopper restarts. `items`: each one's URL and `state` (`closed`, `merged`, the run's conclusion, or `not_found`).

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `items` | object[] | yes |

```json
{
  "items": [
    {
      "url": "https://github.com/octo/identity/issues/199",
      "state": "closed"
    },
    {
      "url": "https://github.com/octo/platform/actions/runs/37998997248",
      "state": "failure"
    }
  ]
}
```

## `job.wait_overdue`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/job.wait_overdue.v1.json`). A job's own wait passed the deadline of its wait check (issue #1694): a day after it began, four hours for a wait on its own command. Once per wait. The job stays on its wait and is listed as stuck on its own wait for a person; the hopper checks it each hour after. `deadline`: the deadline; `result`: what the last check found.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `deadline` | string | yes |
| `result` | string | yes |

```json
{
  "deadline": "2026-10-18T10:00:00.000Z",
  "result": "not ended yet: octo/tools#9"
}
```

## `job.checkpointed`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/job.checkpointed.v1.json`). A checkpoint of a job at work, or of one just parked, or for a fresh read of its transcript (issue #1169), was taken and kept (issue #921): its agent session and its work not pushed, read on `machineId`, scrubbed of secrets. `bytes`: its size compressed. `session`: whether it holds the agent session (without it, the job cannot resume elsewhere). `commits`: the commits not pushed then. Only the latest checkpoint of a job is kept.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `machineId` | string | yes |
| `bytes` | integer | yes |
| `session` | boolean | yes |
| `commits` | integer | yes |

```json
{
  "machineId": "laptop",
  "bytes": 48213,
  "session": true,
  "commits": 2
}
```

## `job.note_added`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/job.note_added.v1.json`). A person, or an agent over the API, sent a note to the job (issue #997, `POST /ui/api/jobs/:id/notes`): `noteId`, its `text`, who (`person`) and how (`via`: `ui`, `api`, `cli`). It is queued on the job (`notes`) until the job's session gets it: at the next turn boundary while it runs, in its task as it starts, with the answer as it resumes. A job that waits — on a question, its own wait, a hold, parked — keeps it queued; a new job of its item carries it (`job.note_carried`).

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `noteId` | string | yes |
| `text` | string | yes |
| `person` | string | yes |
| `via` | `ui` \| `cli` \| `api` | yes |

```json
{
  "noteId": "note-1",
  "text": "The instance is up on port 8443.",
  "person": "ada",
  "via": "ui"
}
```

## `job.note_delivered`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/job.note_delivered.v1.json`). The job's executor typed the queued notes (`noteIds`) into its session (issue #997). `delivery`: `turn` (at a turn boundary while it ran: Claude ready, its turn over, never on a question, a report or a login), `start` (in its task) or `resume` (after the answer it resumed with).

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `noteIds` | string[] | yes |
| `delivery` | `start` \| `turn` \| `resume` | yes |

```json
{
  "noteIds": [
    "note-1"
  ],
  "delivery": "turn"
}
```

## `job.note_carried`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/job.note_carried.v1.json`). A new job of the job's item (run again, rework, I fixed it) took the notes it never delivered (`noteIds`, issue #997): queued on `nextJobId`, `carried` on this job.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `noteIds` | string[] | yes |
| `nextJobId` | string | yes |

```json
{
  "noteIds": [
    "note-1"
  ],
  "nextJobId": "job-2"
}
```

## `job.quarantined`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/job.quarantined.v1.json`). A person, or an agent over the API, quarantined the job (issue #655, `POST /ui/api/jobs/:id/quarantine`): its trust stamp is signed `quarantined`, so the decider holds it, and its proxy token opens no door of the hopper (the GitHub proxy, git, the vault, skills, steps, artifacts, its stream) — a running job keeps its pane, but reaches nothing through the hopper. `was`: its trust level before, the level a lift gives back; absent when its stamp did not verify. `reason` `deny:sandbox`: a person's second deny at gate 2 in the job quarantined it (part 5: a declined sandbox request), or a deny of a job at `untrusted`; `deny:jev`: Jev's deny was the second (part 13). Who (`person`) and how (`via`), or `by` `jev` for Jev's deny.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `was` | `quarantined` \| `untrusted` \| `screened` \| `approved` \| `trusted` \| `owner` | no |
| `reason` | string | no |
| `person` | string | no |
| `via` | `ui` \| `cli` \| `api` | no |
| `by` | `jev` | no |

```json
{
  "was": "trusted",
  "person": "ada",
  "via": "ui"
}
```

## `job.unquarantined`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/job.unquarantined.v1.json`). A person, or an agent with a box token, lifted the job's quarantine (issue #655, `POST /ui/api/jobs/:id/unquarantine`): its stamp is signed at `level` again — the level it had before its quarantine, or the rules' level when none was kept. Who (`person`) and how (`via`).

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `level` | `quarantined` \| `untrusted` \| `screened` \| `approved` \| `trusted` \| `owner` | yes |
| `person` | string | yes |
| `via` | `ui` \| `cli` \| `api` | yes |

```json
{
  "level": "trusted",
  "person": "ada",
  "via": "ui"
}
```

## `job.trust_lowered`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/job.trust_lowered.v1.json`). Jev's trust check (issue #655 part 4, the decision point `intake-trust` active) lowered the job's trust stamp before it started, `from` its level `to` a lower one: a pick with its reason, or — no answer, not sure, Jev not there — `untrusted` (fail closed). `reason`: the reason id added to the stamp (`jev:touches_ci`, `jev:no_answer`). `by`: `jev`. Or (part 5) a person's deny at gate 2 lowered a job one level, `by` `person`, with `reason` `deny:sandbox` (a declined sandbox request), who (`person`) and how (`via`); the second deny in the job quarantines it (`job.quarantined`). Or (part 13) Jev's sandbox check denied a sandbox request, `by` `jev`, with `reason` `deny:jev`; it counts with a person's denies. Or (part 7) a sync saw the item of a started job edited: its stamp drops to `untrusted`, `by` `edit`, with `reason` `edit:text`; the job goes on with the text it started with, and gate 2 then approves nothing for it with no person until a person approves its trust.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `from` | `quarantined` \| `untrusted` \| `screened` \| `approved` \| `trusted` \| `owner` | yes |
| `to` | `quarantined` \| `untrusted` \| `screened` \| `approved` \| `trusted` \| `owner` | yes |
| `reason` | string | yes |
| `by` | `jev` \| `person` \| `edit` | yes |
| `person` | string | no |
| `via` | `ui` \| `cli` \| `api` | no |

```json
{
  "from": "trusted",
  "to": "untrusted",
  "reason": "jev:touches_ci",
  "by": "jev"
}
```

## `job.trust_approved`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/job.trust_approved.v1.json`). A person, or an agent with a box token, approved the trust of a job Jev's trust check, a deny at gate 2 or an edit of its item lowered, or of a job with no item held below approved (issue #655 parts 4, 5 and 7, issue #1974, `POST /ui/api/jobs/:id/approve-trust`): its stamp is signed `approved`, `from` the level it had. Who (`person`) and how (`via`).

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `from` | `quarantined` \| `untrusted` \| `screened` \| `approved` \| `trusted` \| `owner` | yes |
| `person` | string | yes |
| `via` | `ui` \| `cli` \| `api` | yes |

```json
{
  "from": "untrusted",
  "person": "ada",
  "via": "ui"
}
```

## `job.critical_flag_changed`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/job.critical_flag_changed.v1.json`). A person, or an agent over the API, set (`critical` true) or cleared the job's critical flag (issue #2203, `POST /ui/api/jobs/:id/critical`): a job with the flag is a critical job whatever its priority, so the critical job tracker shows it on every page. The lane over the cap stays a rule of the critical priority. `person` and `via` say who acted.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `critical` | boolean | yes |
| `person` | string | yes |
| `via` | `ui` \| `cli` \| `api` | yes |

```json
{
  "critical": true,
  "person": "ada",
  "via": "ui"
}
```

## `intake.stamped`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/intake.stamped.v1.json`). The job store signed the job's trust stamp from where its work came (issue #655 part 11, design.md "Trust stamps"): at its making (`by` `intake`, or `job` for a job a job made), for a new spec (`respecify`), at the backfill of a job made before stamps (`backfill`), or when a sync judged its origin later (`intake`, or `person` when a quarantine stays). `level` and `reasons`: as on the stamp; `was`: a quarantined job's level before it. `from`: the level its stamp verified at before, when it had one. `spec`: the SHA-256 of the spec the stamp covers, as canonical JSON. The MAC is never in it. A job with no stamp (no stamp key, or a parent whose stamp does not verify) has none.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `level` | `quarantined` \| `untrusted` \| `screened` \| `approved` \| `trusted` \| `owner` | yes |
| `reasons` | string[] | yes |
| `by` | `intake` \| `job` \| `respecify` \| `backfill` \| `person` \| `jev` \| `edit` | yes |
| `was` | `quarantined` \| `untrusted` \| `screened` \| `approved` \| `trusted` \| `owner` | no |
| `from` | `quarantined` \| `untrusted` \| `screened` \| `approved` \| `trusted` \| `owner` | no |
| `spec` | string | yes |

```json
{
  "level": "trusted",
  "reasons": [
    "origin:trusted"
  ],
  "by": "intake",
  "spec": "9f2c41d0b7e85a3c6d1e04f7a2b9c8d3e5f6a7b8c9d0e1f2a3b4c5d6e7f8a9b0"
}
```

## `terminal.opened`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/terminal.opened.v1.json`). A person opened a terminal (issue #1128): the job's (`POST /ui/api/jobs/:id/terminal/screen`), or the machine's (`POST /ui/api/machines/:id/terminal/screen`), which names `machineId` and `paneId` and the job only when one holds that pane. It is the first read of the pane by that person, or the first after two minutes with no read or input. `sessionId` names the session; `person` and `via` (`ui`, `api`, `cli`) say who and how.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `sessionId` | string | yes |
| `person` | string | yes |
| `via` | `ui` \| `cli` \| `api` | yes |
| `machineId` | string | no |
| `paneId` | string | no |

```json
{
  "sessionId": "term-1",
  "person": "ada",
  "via": "ui"
}
```

## `terminal.typed`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/terminal.typed.v1.json`). A person typed into a terminal (issue #1128): the job's (`POST /ui/api/jobs/:id/terminal/input`) or the machine's (`POST /ui/api/machines/:id/terminal/input`, with `machineId` and `paneId`), in the session `sessionId`: `chars`, how many characters of text were written to its pane, or `keys`, the key names pressed. The text itself is never in the event: it may hold a secret.

| `via` | `ui` \| `cli` \| `api` | yes |

| `chars` | integer | no |
| `keys` | string[] | no |

```json

  "sessionId": "term-1",
  "person": "ada",
  "via": "ui",
  "chars": 12
}
```

## `source.stalled`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/source.stalled.v1.json`). A job source has been in error since `since` for longer than the stall threshold (30 minutes): nothing new is pulled from it. Recorded once per run of failures; `error` is its last error. The notifiers send it.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `source` | string | yes |
| `kind` | string | yes |
| `error` | string | yes |
| `since` | string | yes |

```json
{
  "source": "github-account",
  "kind": "github-account",
  "error": "GitHub is down",
  "since": "2026-10-07T20:14:00.000Z"
}
```

## `connected_account.expired`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/connected_account.expired.v1.json`). The sign-in of the user's connected account ended: GitHub refused its refresh token itself and no newer pair was stored (revoked, or the app's authorization removed), or the token expired with nothing to renew it (`reason`). A renewal that failed for a reason that may pass (GitHub not answering, a 5xx, a rate limit) never ends it. The account reads as expired until connected again; its source pauses and asks to connect again; nothing reads GitHub in its place. Recorded once. The notifiers send it.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `provider` | `github` | yes |
| `key` | string | no |
| `account` | string | yes |
| `reason` | string | yes |

```json
{
  "provider": "github",
  "account": "octocat",
  "reason": "GitHub refused the refresh token (bad_refresh_token)"
}
```

## `connected_account.renewed`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/connected_account.renewed.v1.json`). The renewer kept a new token for the user's connected account (issue #647): when the new one expires (`expiresAt`; absent: it does not). Never a token. Running jobs are handed the new token on their machines at once.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `provider` | `github` | yes |
| `key` | string | no |
| `account` | string | yes |
| `expiresAt` | string | no |

```json
{
  "provider": "github",
  "account": "octocat",
  "expiresAt": "2026-10-09T18:00:00.000Z"
}
```

## `connected_account.renewal_failed`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/connected_account.renewal_failed.v1.json`). A renewal of the user's connected account failed (issue #647): GitHub's OAuth error (`code`: `bad_refresh_token`, `incorrect_client_credentials`, …), `http_<status>` when GitHub answered with no OAuth error, `renewal_blocked` when this hopper cannot renew it as it is set up, `no_answer` when GitHub did not answer. Never a token. Recorded at each failed try; `connected_account.expired` follows when the failure ends the connection.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `provider` | `github` | yes |
| `key` | string | no |
| `account` | string | yes |
| `code` | string | yes |

```json
{
  "provider": "github",
  "account": "octocat",
  "code": "http_502"
}
```

## `ui_session.ended`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/ui_session.ended.v1.json`). A UI session of the user's ended (issue #439), with the realm it signed in with and why (`reason`): `expired-idle` (no request for the idle timeout), `expired-absolute` (its maximum passed), `refresh-refused` (a gateway realm's session whose forwarded token no longer checks out), `provider-unreachable` (that token's issuer stayed out of reach past the grace period), `realm-changed` (the sign-in config changed: its realm gone or off, or no rule grants it a role), `connection-ended` (signed in with GitHub, and the user's GitHub connection ended: `connected_account.expired`; issue #513 — recorded only before issue #1380, since then a connection that ends ends no session) or `logout`. The session lengths are Settings → Sign-in's.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `reason` | `expired-idle` \| `expired-absolute` \| `refresh-refused` \| `provider-unreachable` \| `realm-changed` \| `connection-ended` \| `logout` | yes |
| `realm` | string | yes |

```json
{
  "reason": "expired-idle",
  "realm": "corp"
}
```

## `source.claim_released`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/source.claim_released.v1.json`). A `hopper:claimed` label (and its `hopper:held-by:<id>` holder label) was removed from an item no job here holds (issue #440). `by: "hopper"`: the claim was this user's own, its job gone — the item is taken again; `by: "migration"`: the intake migration released a claim written before claims named their holder, which no user of this hopper has a job for; `by: "user"`: released from Sources. `reason` says which.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `source` | string | yes |
| `key` | string | yes |
| `by` | `hopper` \| `migration` \| `user` | yes |
| `reason` | string | yes |

```json
{
  "source": "github-account",
  "key": "https://github.com/octocat/hello/issues/7",
  "by": "hopper",
  "reason": "claimed by this user of this hopper, with no job here"
}
```

## `source.request_approved`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/source.request_approved.v1.json`). A person approved a request card (issue #652): an issue not of a trusted origin — `actors` says who wrote, labelled and assigned it (on GitLab also who edited its title or description, `edited`, issue #1642), and whether each is a trusted actor —, whose title and body hash as `hash`. Its text is the item's snapshot (`approved`): the next sync takes it, and its job runs that text. `person` and `via`: who approved it. Never the text.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `source` | string | yes |
| `key` | string | yes |
| `hash` | string | yes |
| `author` | string | yes |
| `person` | string | no |
| `via` | `ui` \| `cli` \| `api` | no |
| `actors` | object[] | yes |

```json
{
  "source": "github-account",
  "key": "https://github.com/octocat/hello/issues/8",
  "hash": "aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa",
  "author": "stranger",
  "person": "octocat",
  "via": "ui",
  "actors": [
    {
      "role": "author",
      "login": "stranger",
      "trusted": false
    },
    {
      "role": "labelled",
      "login": "octocat",
      "trusted": true
    },
    {
      "role": "assigned",
      "login": "octocat",
      "trusted": true
    }
  ]
}
```

## `source.request_auto_approved`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/source.request_auto_approved.v1.json`). The hopper approved a request card a rule of the user's auto-approval matched (issue #1268), as a person's approval does: its text is the item's snapshot (`approved`), the next sync takes it, and its job runs that text. `rule`: `reopened` (a trusted actor or a listed app reopened the issue after its job was done), `author` (a trusted actor wrote it), `app` (a listed app or bot wrote it) or `high-label` (a trusted actor or a listed app added `hopper:high`); `actor`: who did that act. A GitLab card (issue #1642) by `author` or `high-label` only. `actors`: who wrote, labelled and assigned it, as on `source.request_approved`. Never the text.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `source` | string | yes |
| `key` | string | yes |
| `hash` | string | yes |
| `author` | string | yes |
| `rule` | `reopened` \| `author` \| `app` \| `high-label` | yes |
| `actor` | string | yes |
| `actors` | object[] | yes |

```json
{
  "source": "github-account",
  "key": "https://github.com/octocat/hello/issues/8",
  "hash": "aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa",
  "author": "stranger",
  "rule": "high-label",
  "actor": "octocat",
  "actors": [
    {
      "role": "author",
      "login": "stranger",
      "trusted": false
    },
    {
      "role": "labelled",
      "login": "octocat",
      "trusted": true
    }
  ]
}
```

## `source.issue_taken_in`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/source.issue_taken_in.v1.json`). A person took an issue into Intake from the Pull requests view's Not tracked list (issue #1176): an untracked pull request (`pullRequest`) closes it, and it was no work item. The issue (`key`) got the source's label and was assigned to the connected account (`assignee`), as Assign to me assigns. The source syncs at once, and Intake lists the issue: a request card when the label is not a trusted actor's.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `source` | string | yes |
| `key` | string | yes |
| `pullRequest` | string | yes |
| `assignee` | string | yes |

```json
{
  "source": "github-account",
  "key": "https://github.com/octocat/hello/issues/11",
  "pullRequest": "https://github.com/octocat/hello/pull/12",
  "assignee": "octocat"
}
```

## `source.request_declined`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/source.request_declined.v1.json`). A person declined a request card (issue #1035): an issue not of a trusted origin, whose title and body hash as `hash`. It makes no job and leaves the request cards waiting in Intake. `choice` (issue #1710): `close`, the hopper closes the issue as not planned and takes off the source's label, its priority labels and `hopper:done`; `open`, the issue stays open and loses the source's label. Either way one comment on the issue says what the hopper did; these writes are rows in the GitHub outbox, and `source.request_decline_written` follows once GitHub took them. Then the issue comes back only when a person adds the label again. With no `choice` (before issue #1710, or a GitLab card), nothing is written, and an edit to its title or body makes it a request card again. `person` and `via`: who declined it. Never the text.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `source` | string | yes |
| `key` | string | yes |
| `hash` | string | yes |
| `author` | string | yes |
| `person` | string | no |
| `via` | `ui` \| `cli` \| `api` | no |
| `choice` | `close` \| `open` | no |

```json
{
  "source": "github-account",
  "key": "https://github.com/octocat/hello/issues/8",
  "hash": "aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa",
  "author": "stranger",
  "person": "octocat",
  "via": "ui",
  "choice": "open"
}
```

## `source.request_decline_written`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/source.request_decline_written.v1.json`). GitHub took the writes of a person's decline (issue #1710): the labels came off, the comment was posted and, for `choice` `close`, the issue was closed as not planned. From now on the issue's labels and state are the record of the decline, the same on every hopper.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `source` | string | yes |
| `key` | string | yes |
| `hash` | string | yes |
| `choice` | `close` \| `open` | yes |

```json
{
  "source": "github-account",
  "key": "https://github.com/octocat/hello/issues/8",
  "hash": "aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa",
  "choice": "open"
}
```

## `source.request_withdrawn`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/source.request_withdrawn.v1.json`). A request card left Intake with no person's approval or decline (issue #1067, part 4): a sync of `source` that listed every repository of the item no longer offers it — its issue closed, its label or assignee gone, or it is of a trusted origin now. Or a person put an end label on its issue by hand on GitHub (issue #1892): `label` names it, and the label stays. Its work item, waiting for approval, is dropped; offered again, it records `source.request_opened` again. Never the text.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `source` | string | yes |
| `key` | string | yes |
| `label` | string | no |

```json
{
  "source": "github-account",
  "key": "https://github.com/octocat/hello/issues/8"
}
```

## `source.delivery_received`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/source.delivery_received.v1.json`). GitHub sent the hopper a **GitHub delivery** (issue #1079): `event` (`issues`) and `action` (`opened`, `labeled`, `assigned`, …) on `repo`, issue `number`; `delivery` is GitHub's id of it (`X-GitHub-Delivery`). Recorded in the log of each user whose job sources `sources` take `repo` as a job repository: each lists it again at a sync a few seconds later, not after the intake sync interval. Not recorded for a repository no job source of the user takes.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `sources` | string[] | yes |
| `delivery` | string | yes |
| `event` | string | yes |
| `action` | string | no |
| `repo` | string | yes |
| `number` | integer | no |

```json
{
  "sources": [
    "github-account"
  ],
  "delivery": "72d3162e-cc78-11e3-81ab-4c9367dc0958",
  "event": "issues",
  "action": "labeled",
  "repo": "octocat/hello",
  "number": 7
}
```

## `source.review_requested`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/source.review_requested.v1.json`). A pull request in a job repository newly asks for the user's review (issue #1141): a **tagged item** for the reason `review`. `key` is its URL, `author` who wrote it. Recorded once while the request stands: after the user reviews it, a new request records it again. Never the text. It shows on Tagged; webhook subscribers get it like any event.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `source` | string | yes |
| `key` | string | yes |
| `author` | string | yes |

```json
{
  "source": "github-account",
  "key": "https://github.com/octocat/hello/pull/12",
  "author": "hubot"
}
```

## `auth.pending`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/auth.pending.v1.json`). A job or run waits on a login (issue #476): a CLI shows a device code to enter at a URL. Kind `paste_code` (issue #1128): a tool sign-in a person started on the machine (`machineId`), with no job, `run` `sign-in`; the person pastes the code its page shows. It goes to the logins, never to the questions or an escalation level. `run` is the executor or escalation level that waits; `questionId` when it is an escalation level's run for that question. Again, with the same `loginId` and `renewed: true`, when the same tool shows a new code for the same job: a login is updated, never duplicated. The URL and the code are never in an event, a log or a webhook: only a UI session of the user reads them, from `GET /api/logins`. `priority`, `high` (issue #535): the job's live priority, and whether it is at or above the high-priority threshold. `holds` (issue #679): every hold on the level's answer that sent it, strongest first — `guard` (`by` `risk` or `guard`, the `guards` by name), `high_priority`, `auto_answer_off`, `low_confidence` (with the `confidence` and the `threshold`). A risk hold the Decider made (issue #679) carries `decider` in place of `guards`: its `risk`, `categories`, `confidence` and `threshold`, or the `error` it failed with. `host` (issue #698): the host of the URL to open — what asks —, never its path or query. The Grok Bot routine notifier posts it (issue #698).

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `loginId` | string | yes |
| `kind` | `device_code` \| `paste_code` | yes |
| `tool` | string | yes |
| `host` | string | no |
| `expiresAt` | string | yes |
| `intervalSec` | integer | no |
| `run` | string | yes |
| `questionId` | string | no |
| `renewed` | boolean | no |
| `priority` | number | no |
| `high` | boolean | no |

```json
{
  "loginId": "l1",
  "kind": "device_code",
  "tool": "gh",
  "host": "github.com",
  "expiresAt": "2026-10-08T18:15:00.000Z",
  "run": "herdr-claude"
}
```

## `auth.completed`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/auth.completed.v1.json`). The machine went on after the login: the tool proceeded (or ended), and the job works again. `by: requester` (issue #1110): the job that asked for the login said it went through (`sh "$HOPPER_LOGIN" completed`, `POST /job/login`); it may complete a login that had failed.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `loginId` | string | yes |
| `kind` | `device_code` \| `paste_code` | yes |
| `tool` | string | yes |
| `by` | `requester` | no |

```json
{
  "loginId": "l1",
  "kind": "device_code",
  "tool": "gh"
}
```

## `auth.expired`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/auth.expired.v1.json`). The login's code ran out (`expiresAt`) before the machine went on. By the logins setting, the job is then asked for a new code by itself (`renewing: true`, the default since issue #1016), holds for a new code a person asks for, or fails with the reason. The Grok Bot routine notifier posts it.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `loginId` | string | yes |
| `kind` | `device_code` \| `paste_code` | yes |
| `tool` | string | yes |
| `expiresAt` | string | yes |
| `renewing` | boolean | no |

```json
{
  "loginId": "l1",
  "kind": "device_code",
  "tool": "gh",
  "expiresAt": "2026-10-08T18:15:00.000Z"
}
```

## `auth.cancelled`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/auth.cancelled.v1.json`). The user cancelled the login. A herdr job is told to stop waiting for it and to go on without it, or to fail.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `loginId` | string | yes |
| `kind` | `device_code` \| `paste_code` | yes |
| `tool` | string | yes |
| `by` | `user` | yes |

```json
  "loginId": "l1",
  "kind": "device_code",
  "tool": "gh",
  "by": "user"
}
```

## `auth.failed`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/auth.failed.v1.json`). What waited on the login ended first (`reason`: the job ended, the run ended with an error), or, `by: requester` (issue #1110), the job that asked for it said it did not go through, and why.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `loginId` | string | yes |
| `kind` | `device_code` \| `paste_code` | yes |
| `tool` | string | yes |
| `reason` | string | yes |
| `by` | `requester` | no |

```json
  "loginId": "l1",
  "kind": "device_code",
  "tool": "gh",
  "reason": "the job ended: timed out"
}
```

## `auth.reopened`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/auth.reopened.v1.json`). The job that asked for a login said a completed (or dismissed) login does not work after all (issue #1110, `sh "$HOPPER_LOGIN" failed`): the login waits on the user again, with the `reason`, until the job reports a new code (`auth.pending`, `renewed: true`).

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `loginId` | string | yes |
| `kind` | `device_code` \| `paste_code` | yes |
| `tool` | string | yes |
| `reason` | string | yes |

```json
  "kind": "device_code",
  "tool": "codex",
  "reason": "codex login status says not logged in"
}
```

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/auth.dismissed.v1.json`). A person put an open login away (issue #1110, `POST /ui/api/logins/:id/dismiss`), whatever its job does: it leaves the active list, and the run that waited on it stops waiting.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `loginId` | string | yes |
| `kind` | `device_code` \| `paste_code` | yes |
| `tool` | string | yes |
| `by` | `user` | yes |
