{
  "loginId": "l1",
  "kind": "device_code",
  "tool": "gh",
  "by": "user"
}
```

## `job.assessed`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/job.assessed.v1.json`). The failure assessor judged a failed job (issue #509): its error normalised to a `signature`, matched to a known cause (`causeId`), its `class` (`transient`, `shared` or `job`), its `decision` — `retry` (runs again at `retryAt`, within the retry limit), `hold` or `redirect` (grouped into the problem `problemId`; a redirected job runs again at once, kept off the problem's machine), or `person` — with its `reasons` and a `summary` for a person. `attempt`: its run in its chain of retries. `auto: false`: that decision's automatic action is off in the failures settings, so it waits for a person. Once per failed job. `priority`, `high` (issue #535): the job's live priority, and whether it is at or above the high-priority threshold. `holds` (issue #679): every hold on the level's answer that sent it, strongest first — `guard` (`by` `risk` or `guard`, the `guards` by name), `high_priority`, `auto_answer_off`, `low_confidence` (with the `confidence` and the `threshold`). A risk hold the Decider made (issue #679) carries `decider` in place of `guards`: its `risk`, `categories`, `confidence` and `threshold`, or the `error` it failed with.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `recordId` | string | yes |
| `signature` | string | yes |
| `class` | `transient` \| `shared` \| `job` | yes |
| `decision` | `retry` \| `hold` \| `redirect` \| `person` \| `continue` | yes |
| `reasons` | string[] | yes |
| `summary` | string | yes |
| `attempt` | integer | yes |
| `auto` | boolean | yes |
| `causeId` | string | no |
| `problemId` | string | no |
| `retryAt` | string | no |
| `priority` | number | no |
| `high` | boolean | no |

```json
{
  "recordId": "f1",
  "signature": "3f9c2a1b7d4e",
  "class": "shared",
  "decision": "redirect",
  "reasons": [
    "known cause: Disk full",
    "redirected: the job may run on another machine than desk"
  ],
  "summary": "Redirected: Disk full on desk. Ran 1 time on desk. Failed: write: ENOSPC: no space left on device.",
  "attempt": 1,
  "auto": true,
  "causeId": "disk-full",
  "problemId": "p1"
}
```

## `failure.grouped`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/failure.grouped.v1.json`). A failed job was grouped into a problem (issue #509): one shared cause, shown once with the jobs it hit. `opened: true` for the job that opened it. `general: true`: no known cause, flagged because the same signature failed enough items within the grouping window. While it is open, a new job its `scope` covers (a machine, an executor on it, or every machine) is held — or placed on another machine — with the reason `held by problem: <title>`. `affected`: its jobs so far.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `problemId` | string | yes |
| `signature` | string | yes |
| `title` | string | yes |
| `opened` | boolean | yes |
| `general` | boolean | yes |
| `decision` | `hold` \| `redirect` | yes |
| `scope` | object | yes |
| `affected` | integer | yes |

```json
{
  "problemId": "p1",
  "signature": "3f9c2a1b7d4e",
  "title": "Disk full on desk",
  "opened": true,
  "general": false,
  "decision": "redirect",
  "scope": {
    "machineId": "desk"
  },
  "affected": 1
}
```

## `failure.resolved`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/failure.resolved.v1.json`). A problem was resolved (issue #509): by a person (`by: "user"`), or by its check (`by: "check"`: the machine is reachable again, or its disk has room again; for a hopper bug a job reported, issue #1147, the fix landed: the issue of its report closed as completed, and the build of this hopper newer than that close). Its jobs held for it run again through the normal queue (`released` of them), and new jobs are no longer held for it. A person's resolution (issue #623) says who (`person`, and the way, `via` `ui` or `cli`) and keeps their `note`, if any.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `problemId` | string | yes |
| `title` | string | yes |
| `by` | `user` \| `check` | yes |
| `released` | integer | yes |
| `person` | string | no |
| `via` | `ui` \| `cli` \| `api` | no |
| `note` | string | no |

```json
{
  "problemId": "p1",
  "title": "Disk full on desk",
  "by": "check",
  "released": 2
}
```

## `failure.released`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/failure.released.v1.json`). A person released a problem's held jobs (issue #623): `released` of them run again now through the normal queue, each with its own `job.rerun` by the assessor. The problem stays open. `person`: who; `via`: the way, `ui` or `cli`.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `problemId` | string | yes |
| `title` | string | yes |
| `released` | integer | yes |
| `person` | string | yes |
| `via` | `ui` \| `cli` \| `api` | yes |

```json
{
  "problemId": "p1",
  "title": "Disk full on desk",
  "released": 2,
  "person": "operator CLI",
  "via": "cli"
}
```

## `handoff.opened`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/handoff.opened.v1.json`). A failed job was handed off to a person (issue #516): automatic handling has ended for it, and it waits in Failures, Needs a person, until a person resolves it (issue #551) or its item runs again — never dropped by age or a restart. `reason`: `retry_limit` (its retries used up), `person` (a job-specific failure), `auto_off` (its decision's automatic action is off in the failures settings), `not_retried` (a run again the assessor decided was refused), or `dismissed` (its locked entry dismissed with nothing else to end it). `summary` and `recordId`: its assessment. `notify: false`: the failures setting says not to tell anyone, and no webhook delivers it. Once per hand-off. `priority`, `high` (issue #535): the job's live priority, and whether it is at or above the high-priority threshold. `holds` (issue #679): every hold on the level's answer that sent it, strongest first — `guard` (`by` `risk` or `guard`, the `guards` by name), `high_priority`, `auto_answer_off`, `low_confidence` (with the `confidence` and the `threshold`). A risk hold the Decider made (issue #679) carries `decider` in place of `guards`: its `risk`, `categories`, `confidence` and `threshold`, or the `error` it failed with.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `handoffId` | string | yes |
| `reason` | `retry_limit` \| `person` \| `auto_off` \| `not_retried` \| `dismissed` | yes |
| `summary` | string | yes |
| `notify` | boolean | yes |
| `recordId` | string | no |
| `decision` | `retry` \| `hold` \| `redirect` \| `person` \| `continue` | no |
| `class` | `transient` \| `shared` \| `job` | no |
| `priority` | number | no |
| `high` | boolean | no |

```json
{
  "handoffId": "h1",
  "reason": "retry_limit",
  "summary": "Needs a person. Ran 4 times on desk, the last for 2 min. Failed: read ECONNRESET.",
  "notify": true,
  "recordId": "f1",
  "decision": "person",
  "class": "transient"
}
```

## `handoff.closed`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/handoff.closed.v1.json`). A hand-off ended (issue #516): `end` `run_again` (its item ran again, from Needs a person, the Queue, the failure's Retry or its source; `nextJobId` the new job), `continued` (a person resolved it with Continue and its job goes on in its own agent session; `nextJobId` that same job, issue #551), `done_by_hand` (a person did the work themselves; its job ends finished), `wont_do` (a person decided it is not to be done, or no real failure; its locked entry dismissed), `cleared` (closed by the build before #551: a person acknowledged it, its locked entry dismissed), `finished` (its job ended finished: its issue closed as complete); or, found stale by the sweep or at start (issue #529), `superseded` (a newer job of its item exists; `nextJobId` it), `item_closed` (its item is closed at its source), `job_gone` (its job is gone) or `resumed` (its job is live again — a Continue, Push it or a resume took it back to the queue —, issue #1777). A person's resolution names who: `person`, and the way, `via` `ui` or `cli` (issue #623).

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `handoffId` | string | yes |
| `end` | `run_again` \| `continued` \| `done_by_hand` \| `wont_do` \| `cleared` \| `finished` \| `superseded` \| `item_closed` \| `job_gone` \| `resumed` | yes |
| `nextJobId` | string | no |
| `resolution` | `continue` \| `fixed` \| `done_by_hand` \| `wont_do` | no |
| `person` | string | no |
| `via` | `ui` \| `cli` \| `api` | no |

```json
{
  "handoffId": "h1",
  "end": "run_again",
  "nextJobId": "j2",
  "resolution": "fixed"
}
```

## `handoff.checked`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/handoff.checked.v1.json`). What an open hand-off's work shows at its job's source changed (issue #621): the failure assessor asks the source, at once for a new hand-off and then every 10 minutes, for the job's item and the pull requests the job opened or pushed to, and keeps the answer on the hand-off for its card. `item`: `open`, `done` (closed as completed), `closed` (closed any other way) or `gone`. `pullRequests`: how many pull requests of the job's it found. `shipped`: a pull request of the job's merged, or its item closed as completed — then the hand-off closes (`handoff.closed`, `end: "finished"`) and the job ends finished (`job.finished`), its source told so in place of the failure. Only when the answer changed.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `handoffId` | string | yes |
| `item` | `open` \| `done` \| `closed` \| `gone` | yes |
| `pullRequests` | integer | yes |
| `shipped` | boolean | yes |

```json
{
  "handoffId": "h1",
  "item": "open",
  "pullRequests": 1,
  "shipped": true
}
```

## `usage.limits_changed`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/usage.limits_changed.v1.json`). The usage limits were set in the UI (issue #522): `from` the soft and hard limits the decider used, `to` the ones it uses from now on. Each is a fraction of a usage budget, from 0 to 1. `softLanes` (issue #2091; absent on events before it): the lanes a machine keeps from the soft limit to the hard limit.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `from` | object | yes |
| `to` | object | yes |

```json
{
  "from": {
    "soft": 0.7,
    "hard": 0.95,
    "softLanes": 1
  },
  "to": {
    "soft": 0.6,
    "hard": 0.9,
    "softLanes": 2
  }
}
```

## `priority_lanes.changed`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/priority_lanes.changed.v1.json`). The priority lanes changed (issue #535): `from` and `to` the lanes high-priority jobs get first, best first. `by`: `reliability` (the hopper measured its lanes again and a lane became more reliable by more than the margin, or one dropped out), `manual` (an admin chose them), `settings` (a settings change, such as the count).

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `from` | string[] | yes |
| `to` | string[] | yes |
| `by` | `reliability` \| `manual` \| `settings` | yes |

  "from": [],
  "to": [
    "desk/lane-1"
  ],
  "by": "reliability"
}
```

## `priority_lanes.settings_changed`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/priority_lanes.settings_changed.v1.json`). An admin saved the priority lane settings (issue #535): `from` and `to` the high-priority threshold, the count of priority lanes, what a priority lane does while no high-priority job waits (`keep-free` or `share`), the window and the minimum runs lane reliability is measured over, and the lanes an admin chose (`manual`; absent: by reliability).

|---|---|---|
| `from` | object | yes |
| `to` | object | yes |

  "from": {
    "highPriority": 75,
    "count": 1,
    "whenIdle": "keep-free",
    "windowDays": 14,
    "minRuns": 5
  },
  "to": {
    "highPriority": 75,
    "count": 2,
    "whenIdle": "share",
    "windowDays": 14,
    "minRuns": 5
  }
}
```

## `proposal.asked`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/proposal.asked.v1.json`). A person asked a job that has not started for a proposal (issue #537): when it starts, its agent is told to write one instead of doing the work. A job from an item labelled `hopper:proposal` is asked from the start, with no event. `by` `user`: a person asked; `jev`: Jev's kind check (issue #655, the decision point `intake-kind`, active) asked a work job from a job source before its first start.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `by` | `user` \| `jev` | yes |

```json
{
  "by": "user"
}
```

## `proposal.submitted`

Version 2 (`docs/schemas/proposal.submitted.v2.json`). A job came back with a proposal (issue #537): its agent ended with HOPPER_PROPOSAL instead of doing the work. Version 1, or the next version of one sent back. The job waits on it. v2 (issue #651): a proposal is a set of paths; `tldr`: its TL;DR, Markdown source (issue #569), `paths`: how many paths it has, `missing`: the parts it left out (TL;DR, Problem, Paths, Recommended, Context). v1: `goal`, its Goal part.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `proposalId` | string | yes |
| `version` | integer | yes |
| `raisedBy` | object | no |
| `priority` | number | no |
| `high` | boolean | no |
| `tldr` | string | no |
| `missing` | `tldr` \| `problem` \| `paths` \| `recommended` \| `context`[] | yes |
| `paths` | integer | no |

```json
{
  "proposalId": "p1",
  "version": 1,
  "tldr": "Cache the board renders: path 1 is small and safe.",
  "missing": [
    "context"
  ],
  "paths": 3,
  "raisedBy": {
    "machineId": "desk",
    "name": "Desk tower",
    "laneId": "desk/lane-1"
  },
  "priority": 50,
  "high": false
}
```

## `proposal.reviewed`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/proposal.reviewed.v1.json`). A reviewer level gave its verdict on a proposal (issue #537): `approve`, `request_changes` or `escalate`, with its `notes`. `error`: the review failed, which escalates. `paths` (issue #651): the paths the level added to the proposal and those it found not viable, by id, before a person sees them.

| field | type | required |

{
  "proposalId": "p1",

## `proposal.revision_requested`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/proposal.revision_requested.v1.json`). A proposal was sent back to its job (issue #537), by a reviewer level or a person (`stage`; `by` names the person): `decision` `request_changes` (a level, or the structural pre-check: `notes` is what to change), `more_paths` (a person asks for more paths, issue #651: the job keeps its paths and their numbers and adds new ones; `notes` is optional) or `steer` (a person sends a note back: `notes`). A selection the person made so far is kept on the proposal for the next version. The job is re-queued with it and writes the next version.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `proposalId` | string | yes |
| `version` | integer | yes |
| `raisedBy` | object | no |
| `priority` | number | no |
| `high` | boolean | no |
| `stage` | string | yes |
| `decision` | `accept` \| `reject` \| `request_changes` \| `dig_deeper` \| `steer` \| `more_paths` | no |
| `notes` | string | yes |
| `by` | string | no |

```json
{
  "proposalId": "p1",
  "version": 1,
  "stage": "opus",
  "decision": "request_changes",
  "notes": "Say how the cache is invalidated."
}
```

## `proposal.accepted`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/proposal.accepted.v1.json`). A proposal was signed off as accepted (issue #537), by a person (`stage: "human"`, `by` who), by the top reviewer level where the proposal settings let it, or by the hopper itself (`stage: "hopper"`, issues #1059, #1174: one recommended path, or each of a recommended combination, and no rule needs a person). `selected` (issue #651): the paths the person continues with, each with its note (the top level continues with the recommended paths); none on a proposal of zero paths. Its job ends finished, with the decision as its result; each selected path continues as a follow-on job (`proposal.followed_on`).

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `proposalId` | string | yes |
| `version` | integer | yes |
| `raisedBy` | object | no |
| `priority` | number | no |
| `high` | boolean | no |
| `stage` | string | yes |
| `by` | string | no |
| `notes` | string | no |
| `then` | `work` \| `end` \| `proposal` | no |
| `selected` | object[] | no |

```json
{
  "proposalId": "p1",
  "version": 2,
  "stage": "human",
  "by": "owner",
  "notes": "Go ahead.",
  "selected": [
    {
      "id": "1",
      "note": "Keep the cache per user."
    },
    {
      "id": "3"
    }
  ]
}
```

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/machine.discovered.v1.json`).     }
  }
}
```

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/blast_radius.settings_changed.v1.json`). An admin saved the blast-radius settings (issue #542): `from` and `to` where the gate stands (`gateAt`), what passes it (`pass`), the rating rules (`rules`), the actor machines and how often each machine is discovered (`everyMinutes`).

A WSL machine's client found that Windows does not reach the hopper (issue #712): Windows, through PowerShell, opened `url` (the address check, `/job/address`, at localhost, at the port the client dials the hopper on; the health route at localhost before it) and got no answer. `error` says why; `mode` is WSL's networking mode (`nat`, `mirrored`), when read. The Machines view and a banner show the fix.   "machineId": "win-desk",
  "url": "http://localhost:4790/job/address",

  "error": "Unable to connect to the remote server"
}
```

## `machine.disk_over_budget`

What is left is work not pushed, live jobs' work, the repository checkouts (the sweep never removes one), or more than the budget allows. Once while it stays over.

  "budgetBytes": 50000000000,

    },
    {
      "path": "/home/me/jobs/.worktrees",
      "bytes": 12000000000
    }
  ]
}
```

## `minor_decision.picked`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/minor_decision.picked.v1.json`). Jev was asked for a decider call (issue #550) at a decision point (`point`: `question-risk`, `failure-assessment`, `lane-count`, `job-machine`, `intake-order`, `merge-order`, `intake-trust`, `intake-kind`, `sandbox-request`; `question-answer` only in events from before issue #679) and picked one of its `options` with a `confidence` — or could not (`error`). A `question-risk` pick (issue #679) is the risk call on a level's answer: `pick` is the risk (`none`, `low`, `real`) and `categories` its kinds (`credentials`, `destructive`, `publish`, `pay`, `permissions`, `ci`, `data`, `other`). `applied`: the pick was acted on (the point is active, the pick met its `threshold`, and nothing made it consequential); otherwise `notApplied` says why (`shadow`, `below_threshold`, `consequential` with what made it so, `no_pick`, `too_late`: decided before Jev answered, and compared at once) and the decision went on as before. A question's pick names it (`questionId`); a `lane-count` pick its machine (`machineId`).

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `pickId` | string | yes |
| `point` | `question-risk` \| `failure-assessment` \| `lane-count` \| `job-machine` \| `intake-order` \| `merge-order` \| `intake-trust` \| `intake-kind` \| `sandbox-request` \| `question-answer` | yes |
| `by` | string | yes |
| `options` | object[] | yes |
| `pick` | string | no |
| `confidence` | number | no |
| `error` | string | no |
| `categories` | `credentials` \| `destructive` \| `publish` \| `pay` \| `permissions` \| `ci` \| `data` \| `other`[] | no |
| `mode` | `off` \| `shadow` \| `active` | yes |
| `threshold` | number | yes |
| `applied` | boolean | yes |
| `notApplied` | `shadow` \| `below_threshold` \| `consequential` \| `no_pick` \| `too_late` | no |
| `consequential` | string[] | no |
| `questionId` | string | no |
| `machineId` | string | no |

```json
{
  "pickId": "p1",
  "point": "question-answer",
  "by": "jev",
  "options": [
    {
      "id": "1",
      "label": "Yes, proceed"
    },
    {
      "id": "2",
      "label": "No"
    }
  ],
  "pick": "1",
  "confidence": 0.91,
  "mode": "shadow",
  "threshold": 0.85,
  "applied": false,
  "notApplied": "shadow",
  "questionId": "q1"
}
```

## `minor_decision.compared`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/minor_decision.compared.v1.json`). What was decided after Jev's pick was not applied (issue #550): `actual`, by `decidedBy` (an escalation level, `human`, `person` for a failed job, or `rules` for an ordering the rules made without Jev, issue #796, or for what the keyword risk rules said of a `question-risk` pick, issue #679: `real` when one matched, else `none`; a `low` risk agrees with `none`), and whether it `agreed` with Jev's `pick`. Feeds the decision point's agreement rate.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `pickId` | string | yes |
| `point` | `question-risk` \| `failure-assessment` \| `lane-count` \| `job-machine` \| `intake-order` \| `merge-order` \| `intake-trust` \| `intake-kind` \| `sandbox-request` \| `question-answer` | yes |
| `pick` | string | yes |
| `actual` | string | yes |
| `agreed` | boolean | yes |
| `decidedBy` | string | yes |

```json
{
  "pickId": "p1",
  "point": "question-answer",
  "pick": "1",
  "actual": "1",
  "agreed": true,
  "decidedBy": "level-1"
}
```

## `minor_decision.overridden`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/minor_decision.overridden.v1.json`). A person said what a decider call should have been (issue #550): `actual` in place of Jev's `pick`. Counts as a disagreement in the agreement rate unless it names Jev's pick.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `pickId` | string | yes |
| `point` | `question-risk` \| `failure-assessment` \| `lane-count` \| `job-machine` \| `intake-order` \| `merge-order` \| `intake-trust` \| `intake-kind` \| `sandbox-request` \| `question-answer` | yes |
| `pick` | string | no |
| `actual` | string | yes |

```json
{
  "pickId": "p1",
  "point": "failure-assessment",
  "pick": "retry",
  "actual": "person"
}
```

| `point` | `question-risk` \| `failure-assessment` \| `lane-count` \| `job-machine` \| `intake-order` \| `merge-order` \| `intake-trust` \| `intake-kind` \| `sandbox-request` \| `question-answer` | yes |

## `job.phase_changed`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/job.phase_changed.v1.json`). A job moved into another phase (issue #548): `from` and `to` are `work`, `research` or `proposal`. A switch from a question (`mode: "switch"`, the `questionId`, the person or level `by`, the scoping `note`) moves it into research or a proposal in the same session; accepted, the person picks whether it goes back to `work`, ends, or goes on from research to a proposal. `reason`: the note, or what moved it.

| `from` | `work` \| `research` \| `proposal` | yes |
| `to` | `work` \| `research` \| `proposal` | yes |

| `note` | string | no |
| `by` | string | no |

  "from": "work",
  "to": "research",

## `job.forked`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/job.forked.v1.json`). A separate research or proposal job (`forkId`) was spun off a job's question (issue #548), by a person or an escalation level the phase-shift settings allow (`by`), about the aspect in `note`. The parent keeps waiting on its question (`parent: "waiting"`) or was parked (`"parked"`). The fork carries the parent's priority; its accepted result answers the question.

| field | type | required |

## `job.fork_resolved`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/job.fork_resolved.v1.json`). A fork's research report or proposal was decided (issue #548). Accepted, it is the answer to the parent's question when that is still open (`delivered`); rejected, the question stays open. `question`: the question's status at the decision (issue #570): `answered` when a person or a level answered it while the fork ran, and an acceptance delivered nothing.

|---|---|---|

  "forkId": "j2",
  "kind": "research",
  "questionId": "q1",

A person kept a new version of a library skill (issue #1911): `name`, its content id `version` and its place `seq` (1, 2, …); `source` says whether a person wrote it (`created`) copied it from another skill's version (`duplicated`, with that `name` and `version`), or imported it from a folder of a GitHub repository (`imported`: `repo`, the folder `path` — empty: the root —, the `ref` it follows, the `commit` read). Never its files: GET /api/skill-library/{name} answers them.

    "kind": "created"
  },

The next job gets it, never a running one.

|---|---|---|
| `from` | object | yes |

## `job.work_skill_chosen`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/job.work_skill_chosen.v1.json`). The work skill this job got (issue #1911), at its first start or when its kind of work changed: its kind of work (`code`, `research`, `proposal`), the skill `name`, its `version` and `seq` (0: built in), and which setting chose it (`repo`, `user`, `default`). `requires`: the skills it got beside it because the work skill, or a skill it requires, names them in its SKILL.md's `requires:` — each `name`, `version` and `seq`; `missing`: the ones required that it did not get (not in the library, or past the limit of 8). Both absent on a choice made before skills required others. Each later start of the job, on any machine, gets the same versions.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `kind` | `code` \| `research` \| `proposal` | yes |
| `name` | string | yes |
| `version` | string | yes |
| `seq` | integer | yes |
| `from` | `repo` \| `user` \| `default` | yes |
| `requires` | object[] | no |
| `missing` | string[] | no |

```json
{
  "kind": "code",
  "name": "careful-work",
  "version": "3f9c2a7b1d4e6f80",
  "seq": 2,
  "from": "user",
  "requires": [
    {
      "name": "work",
      "version": "8a1d3c5e7f9b2d40",
      "seq": 0
    }
  ],
  "missing": []
}
```

## `job.conditional_skills_chosen`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/job.conditional_skills_chosen.v1.json`). The conditional skills this job got beside its work skill (issue #1924), at its first start, because a skill rule matched what it works on: each skill's `name`, `version` and `seq` (0: built in), `why` (the conditions that matched: `repository owner/name`, `label x`, `kind of work k`, `paths a, b`), and `done`, the done criteria of its `done.json` that the done check verifies before the job is done (part 3: `person-merges`, a person merges a change to its `paths`, never the hopper's yolo mode, which reads the criteria again before its merge). `paths` (part 2): the globs of a paths rule; the done check verifies the criteria only when the pull request changes a file they match. Absent: always. Each later start gets the same versions. None when no rule matched.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `skills` | object[] | yes |

```json
{
  "skills": [
    {
      "name": "iac",
      "version": "9a1c3e5f7b2d4068",
      "seq": 0,
      "why": [
        "repository owner/infra"
      ],
      "done": [
        {
          "kind": "checks-passed",
          "checks": "terraform plan*"
        },
        {
          "kind": "plan-destroy",
          "checks": "terraform plan*"
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

## `job.preempted`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/job.preempted.v1.json`). A Decision preempted this running job (issue #1525): job `by`, of priority `byPriority`, waits for a lane, every lane it may use is busy, and this job has the lower priority `priority`. It is parked next (`job.parked`), its lane frees, and it is queued again (`job.unparked`) to resume where it stopped. `reason`: the Decision's.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `by` | string | yes |
| `byPriority` | number | yes |
| `priority` | number | yes |
| `reason` | string | yes |

```json
{
  "by": "j-high",
  "byPriority": 75,
  "priority": 50,
  "reason": "preempts j-low (priority 50, running 42 min) on laptop/lane-2: job j-high of priority 75 waits and every lane it may use is busy"
}
```

## `job.memory_paused`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/job.memory_paused.v1.json`). A Decision paused this running job (issue #2291): its machine has `availableBytes` of memory available, below its memory floor `floorBytes`, and this job started there last. It is parked next (`job.parked`), its lane and memory free, and it is queued again (`job.unparked`) to resume there where it stopped once the memory holds it. `reason`: the Decision's.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `availableBytes` | number | yes |
| `floorBytes` | number | yes |
| `reason` | string | yes |

```json
{
  "availableBytes": 1073741824,
  "floorBytes": 1503238554,
  "reason": "pauses j-new on laptop/lane-6: laptop has 1 GiB available, below its floor of 1.4 GiB; j-new started there last"
}
```

## `job.wait_released`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/job.wait_released.v1.json`). A Decision ended the agent of this job on its own wait (issues #2303, #2326), on its machine (`machineId`): the hopper ends this wait by itself, with no pane, and a waiting job holds no agent. Its pane and agent end next and its checkpoint is taken; it stays on its wait, its work tree and agent session kept (`waitReleased` on the job). When its wait ends, it resumes its session from that checkpoint on any machine with room, else in a new pane on its machine. `reason`: the Decision's.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `reason` | string | yes |

```json
{
  "reason": "releases the agent of j-wait on laptop: it waits on its own since 42 min ago, and a waiting job holds no agent; it resumes its session when its wait ends, on any machine with room"
}
```

The hopper's admin changed the shared rate limiter's settings (issue #436): below which share of a GitHub rate limit, in percent, calls are spread to its reset (`slowBelowPercent`), how many calls are kept in reserve (`reserve`), how many polls run at once in a batch (`batchSize`), and how many calls intake leaves for job work (`intakeReserve`, issue #983), how often intake lists the job repositories, in minutes (`intakeSyncMinutes`, issue #985), and how often the in-motion cycle reads the pull requests in motion, in minutes (`prCycleMinutes`, issue #985); each absent from a change made before it. `from` and `to`. An instance event: in every user's log.

|---|---|---|

| `to` | object | yes |

## `remote_access.changed`

Version 2 (`docs/schemas/remote_access.changed.v2.json`). The hopper's admin changed remote access (issues #880, #968), `from` and `to`: on or off (`enabled`); the provider picked (`provider`: `cloudflare` or `ngrok`); the host name asked for (`domain`); when the admin last started the tunnel again (`restartedAt`); what the hopper minted at the provider (`provisioned`: the host name, and the ids it removes again — at Cloudflare the account, zone, tunnel and DNS record, at ngrok the tunnel credential and a domain it reserved; none of them a secret); `leftover`: what a release could not remove at the provider. `credential`: the provider's credential was `set` or `removed` (never its value: it is the system secret `remote-access.cloudflare-api-token` or `remote-access.ngrok-api-key`). `by` is `hopper` when a start moved NGROK_AUTHTOKEN from the environment. An instance event: in every user's log.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `from` | object | yes |
| `to` | object | yes |
| `credential` | `set` \| `removed` | no |
| `by` | string | yes |

```json
{
  "from": {
    "enabled": false,
    "provider": "cloudflare"
  },
  "to": {
    "enabled": true,
    "provider": "cloudflare",
    "provisioned": {
      "provider": "cloudflare",
      "domain": "hopper.example.com",
      "accountId": "a1b2",
      "zoneId": "z3c4",
      "tunnelId": "f1e2d3c4-0000-4000-8000-000000000000",
      "dnsRecordId": "r5d6"
    }
  },
  "credential": "set",
  "by": "admin"
}
```

The link's state is `pending` again and its `registeredAt` is gone; the link record stays, and nothing else on the instance changes. A new registration code registers it again, with the same id. `installId` and `account`, the link. An instance event: in every user's log.

The instance refused a message hopper.io sent over the cloud link (issue #465): it was larger than 1024 bytes (`too-large`), not JSON (`not-json`), of a type other than `register` or `unregister` (`unknown-type`), or not of that type's closed shape (`bad-shape`); or one too many in a minute (`too-many`), which also closes the connection. Nothing changed on the instance. `reason`, why; never the message. An instance event: in every user's log.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|

The cloud link connected to hopper.io (issue #2039, design.md "The cloud link's connection"): the instance checked hopper.io by TLS and the pin of its key, its hello proved the cloud link key, and hopper.io took it. From here the instance sends its heartbeat and, while registered, its state snapshot. `installId` and `account`, the link. An instance event: in every user's log.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|

## `cloud_link.disconnected`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/cloud_link.disconnected.v1.json`). The cloud link's connection to hopper.io ended (issue #2039): it was lost, hopper.io closed it, or an unlink, a key change or a stop closed it. The agent tries again with backoff (1 second, doubling, at most 5 minutes) while the link record exists. `installId` and `account`, the link; `code`, the WebSocket close code (`1000` closed by the instance, `1006` lost, `4000` another connection of this instance took its place). An instance event: in every user's log.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `installId` | string | yes |
| `account` | string | yes |
| `code` | integer | yes |

```json
{
  "installId": "a1b2c3d4e5f60718",
  "account": "octo-cat",
  "code": 1006
}
```

## `cloud_link.connection_refused`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/cloud_link.connection_refused.v1.json`). A connection to hopper.io was refused (issue #2039): by the instance before its hello — hopper.io's key does not match the pin in the code (`pin`), its certificate is not good (`tls`), or it answered with no WebSocket (`http`) — or by hopper.io after the hello: too many connections (`too-many`), a hello it does not take (`bad-hello`), another key than the one its registration holds (`unknown-key`), or no hello in time (`hello-timeout`). Recorded once while the same refusal repeats. `installId` and `account`, the link; `reason`, why. An instance event: in every user's log.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `installId` | string | yes |
| `account` | string | yes |
| `reason` | `pin` \| `tls` \| `http` \| `too-many` \| `bad-hello` \| `unknown-key` \| `hello-timeout` | yes |

```json
{
  "installId": "a1b2c3d4e5f60718",
  "account": "octo-cat",
  "reason": "pin"
}
```

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/cloud_link.revoked.v1.json`). The cloud link key was revoked (issue #2039, docs/hopper-io-security.md R4): by hopper.io (`by` is `hopper.io`), when its account owner removed this instance there or deleted the account — the agent does not connect again until the admin rotates the key —, or by the hopper's admin on this instance (`by`, who), which drops the key and keeps the link with no key until a rotation. `installId` and `account`, the link. An instance event: in every user's log.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `installId` | string | yes |
| `account` | string | yes |
| `by` | string | yes |

```json
{
  "installId": "a1b2c3d4e5f60718",
  "account": "octo-cat",
  "by": "hopper.io"
}
```

## `cloud_link.message_dropped`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/cloud_link.message_dropped.v1.json`). The instance did not send a message to hopper.io (issue #2039, docs/hopper-io-security.md R4, R7): the outgoing scan found a secret in it (`secret`), or it was over its cap (`too-large`: 1024 bytes, or the snapshot's 192 KiB). Nothing of it left the instance. `message`, which kind; `reason`, why; never the message. An instance event: in every user's log.

| `message` | `hello` \| `heartbeat` \| `snapshot` \| `registration` \| `unregistration` \| `refused` \| `unlinked` | yes |
| `reason` | `secret` \| `too-large` | yes |

  "message": "snapshot",
  "reason": "secret"
}
```

## `github_proxy.done`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/github_proxy.done.v1.json`). The hopper did a GitHub operation a running job asked for (issue #563), with the GitHub connection of the job's own user (issue #1380): `op` (`issue.create`, `issue.comment`, `issue.view`, `issue.comments`, `issue.close`, `pr.create`, `pr.view`, `pr.diff`, `pr.commits`, `pr.checks`, `pr.reviews`, `pr.status`, `pr.ready`, `pr.edit`, `pr.close`; issue #1734: a pull request the job opened, or its work item's) on `repo`, `number` and `url` where it is; for a read (a repo query, issue #1074), `source`: `github` when GitHub was read for it, `cache` when the hopper's repo-query cache answered it, `hopper` when its records answered it (issue #1072, `pr.status`: the Pull requests list and the work-item ledger); for a `pr wait` (issue #1072 part 2, asked as `pr.status`), `wait`: the id of the watch it opened on the job's stream while the checks run, `settled` when they had ended, or `none` when the hopper does not follow the pull request — with `--for mergeable` (issue #1210) the watch waits for the next mergeability the hopper sees instead —; `poll` (issue #1210): the job asked the same read this many times in 15 minutes, a poll of hopper state, and the answer told it to wait through the hopper; a repository read or forked (issue #429, `repo.view`, `repo.fork`): its `url`, and for a fork `fork`, the fork made or found in the user's account; a failed check's log read (issue #993, `check.log`): `number`, its GitHub Actions job, and `url`, its check run (the log itself is never in the event); a repository's workflow runs read (issue #2318, `run.list`): `url`, its Actions page, and no `number`; a run and its jobs read (`run.view`): `number`, the run's id, and `url`, the run; or the job's git push (issue #652, op `git.push`, with the connection of the job's own user): `refs`, the refs it changed, and no `number` or `url`; `heads` (issue #2087), the commit each ref moved to, so the reap and the sweep read that work as pushed; `direct` (issue #1806), the refs it moved straight on the repository's target branch with direct push on, each a fast-forward. `key` (issue #1607, `issue.create` and `issue.comment`; issue #1959 part 4, `pr.create`): the **resend key** hopper-gh sent with it; the same request sent again with that key is answered from this event, and nothing is done again on GitHub; that answer is recorded as `github_proxy.done` again, with `replayed`. `found` (issue #1959 part 2): the issue, comment or pull request (part 4) was found on GitHub by its **post key**, made by an earlier send of the same key that a hopper killed before it recorded it; nothing was made again. `requestId` names the request (an issue filed this way says it at its end); `machine`, the job's machine; `as` (issue #1380), the GitHub login that acted for the job, its own user's connected account. Events recorded before issue #1380 carry `own` (the job was the hopper's oldest user's) and, for another user's job, a copy in the oldest user's log with `forUser` and `job`.

`data` is `{}`.

```json
{
  "requestId": "r1",
  "machine": "desk",
  "as": "octocat",
  "op": "issue.create",
  "repo": "octo/tools",
  "number": 42,
  "url": "https://github.com/octo/tools/issues/42"
}
```

## `github_proxy.refused`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/github_proxy.refused.v1.json`). The hopper refused a GitHub operation a running job asked for (issue #563), and told the job `reason`: a request it does not take, a repository it does not work on, a rate limit, or no GitHub connection of the job's user; for a git push (issue #652), a push to another repository than the job's own (or, with Contribution on, its user's fork of it, issue #429), to one its user cannot push to, or to its default or a release branch, a tag or a delete; or a push the **shrink guard** refused (issue #1096): it brings in the default branch and empties or shrinks files the branch's own change does not, named in `shrunk` (`path`, its lines `from` — on the base branch, or `against: head` before the push — and `to`). Fields as `github_proxy.done`; `op` and `repo` when the request named them, and a push's `refs` when it was read.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `requestId` | string | yes |
| `machine` | string | no |
| `as` | string | no |
| `own` | boolean | no |
| `forUser` | string | no |
| `job` | string | no |
| `op` | string | no |
| `repo` | string | no |
| `refs` | string[] | no |
| `reason` | string | yes |
| `shrunk` | object[] | no |

```json
{
  "requestId": "r2",
  "machine": "box",
  "as": "octocat",
  "op": "issue.create",
  "repo": "else/where",
  "reason": "else/where is not one of the repositories the hopper works on, so it does nothing there for a job but open a pull request from a branch it pushed"
}
```

GitHub failed or refused a GitHub operation the hopper did for a running job (issue #563): `error` is what GitHub answered, as the job was told; for a git push a hopper stopped during (issue #1806, a push kept as a saga), the refs GitHub does not have, recorded by the next hopper. | `repo` | string | yes |
| `refs` | string[] | no |
| `error` | string | yes |

## `github_proxy.sending`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/github_proxy.sending.v1.json`). A running job's issue create, comment or pull request create (part 4) with a **resend key** (issue #1607) is on its way to GitHub (issue #1959 part 2): `op` (`issue.create`, `issue.comment`, `pr.create`), `repo`, `number` (the issue a comment goes on) and `key`. Recorded before the call, so a hopper killed before it recorded the answer leaves it: the same key sent again then looks for the issue, comment or pull request (from the same head) on GitHub by its **post key** first, and makes it only when it is not there. Fields as `github_proxy.done`.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `requestId` | string | yes |
| `machine` | string | no |
| `as` | string | no |
| `own` | boolean | no |
| `forUser` | string | no |
| `job` | string | no |
| `op` | `issue.create` \| `issue.comment` \| `pr.create` | yes |
| `repo` | string | yes |
| `number` | integer | no |
| `key` | string | yes |

```json
{
  "requestId": "r4",
  "machine": "desk",
  "as": "octocat",
  "op": "issue.comment",
  "repo": "octo/tools",
  "number": 42,
  "key": "5f0c9a2b7d1e4c3a8b6f0e21"
}
```

## `gitlab_proxy.done`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/gitlab_proxy.done.v1.json`). A GitLab job's git push went through the hopper to GitLab (issue #1448 part 3, design.md "Jobs through GitLab"), with the token of the GitLab account of the job's own user: `project`, the job's own GitLab project; `refs`, the refs it changed (git's push options, such as `merge_request.create`, went with it); `heads` (issue #2087), the commit each ref moved to, so the reap reads that work as pushed; `as`, the GitLab username that acted; `requestId` names the request; `machine`, the job's machine.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `requestId` | string | yes |
| `machine` | string | no |
| `as` | string | no |
| `op` | string | yes |
| `project` | string | yes |
| `refs` | string[] | yes |
| `heads` | string[] | no |

```json
{
  "requestId": "r4",
  "machine": "desk",
  "as": "ada",
  "op": "git.push",
  "project": "ada/tools",
  "refs": [
    "refs/heads/fix-parser"
  ],
  "heads": [
    "3f2a9c1d0e4b5a6c7d8e9f0a1b2c3d4e5f6a7b8c"
  ]
}
```

## `gitlab_proxy.refused`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/gitlab_proxy.refused.v1.json`). The hopper refused a GitLab job's git push (issue #1448 part 3) and told the job `reason`: a push to another project than the job's own, to its default or a release branch, a tag or a delete, or no GitLab account to push with. Fields as `gitlab_proxy.done`; `refs` when the push was read.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `requestId` | string | yes |
| `machine` | string | no |
| `as` | string | no |
| `op` | string | yes |
| `project` | string | yes |
| `refs` | string[] | no |
| `reason` | string | yes |

```json
{
  "requestId": "r5",
  "machine": "desk",
  "as": "ada",
  "op": "git.push",
  "project": "ada/tools",
  "refs": [
    "refs/heads/main"
  ],
  "reason": "a job pushes only to a branch of its own work, never to main: push a new branch and open a merge request"
}
```

## `gitlab_proxy.failed`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/gitlab_proxy.failed.v1.json`). GitLab failed or refused a GitLab job's git push the hopper made (issue #1448 part 3): `error` is what GitLab answered; a refused token ends the GitLab account. Fields as `gitlab_proxy.done`.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `requestId` | string | yes |
| `machine` | string | no |
| `as` | string | no |
| `op` | string | yes |
| `project` | string | yes |
| `refs` | string[] | no |
| `error` | string | yes |

```json
{
  "requestId": "r6",
  "machine": "desk",
  "as": "ada",
  "op": "git.push",
  "project": "ada/tools",
  "refs": [
    "refs/heads/fix-parser"
  ],
  "error": "GitLab answered 500"
}
```

## `vault.secret_set`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/vault.secret_set.v1.json`). A vault secret was set (issue #558): `replaced` when it already held a value. Its name and who set it; never its value. `backend`: the vault backend it is kept in (issue #585), when it is kept in one: the hopper holds no value for it. `rotated`: a system secret (issue #658) the hopper made or renewed itself — a webhook secret rotated, a GitHub token renewed. `mints`: the AWS account or cluster it is a minting credential for (issue #580).

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | yes |
| `by` | string | yes |
| `replaced` | boolean | yes |
| `rotated` | boolean | no |
| `backend` | string | no |
| `mints` | object | no |

```json
{
  "name": "KUBE_TOKEN",
  "by": "Ada",
  "replaced": false
}
```

## `vault.secret_removed`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/vault.secret_removed.v1.json`). A vault secret was removed (issue #558), and who removed it.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | yes |
| `by` | string | yes |

```json
{
  "name": "KUBE_TOKEN",
  "by": "Ada"
}
```

## `vault.secret_read`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/vault.secret_read.v1.json`). The hopper read one of its own secrets in the vault's system scope (issue #658), for `purpose`: at most once an hour per secret, since some are read at every source poll. `by` is always `hopper`: no job reads a system secret. Never the value.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | yes |
| `by` | string | yes |
| `purpose` | string | no |

```json
{
  "name": "system/connected-account.github.access-token",
  "by": "hopper",
  "purpose": "github"
}
```

## `vault.secret_migrated`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/vault.secret_migrated.v1.json`). One of the hopper's own secrets moved into the vault's system scope at start (issue #658), from where it was kept before (`from`: `connected_accounts`, `webhooks`, `sign-in`); it was opened again before the old copy was removed. Never the value.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | yes |
| `from` | string | yes |

```json
{
  "name": "system/webhook.3f2c.signing-secret",
  "from": "webhooks"
}
```

## `vault.master_key_rotated`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/vault.master_key_rotated.v1.json`). The hopper's admin rotated the master key (issue #659): every secret the old key sealed, in every vault, was sealed again under a new key in one transaction (`resealed`); `unreadable` counts the ones the old key sealed that did not open, left as they were. `from` and `to` are the two keys' short fingerprints, never a key; `by` pressed it. The new key is shown once, to them. Appended to every user's log.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `from` | string | yes |
| `to` | string | yes |
| `by` | string | yes |
| `resealed` | integer | yes |
| `unreadable` | integer | yes |

```json
{
  "from": "9c1e04b7a2d35f60",
  "to": "4b7d2e91c0a6f358",
  "by": "admin",
  "resealed": 12,
  "unreadable": 0
}
```

## `template.saved`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/template.saved.v1.json`). A template was saved (issue #558): its image, the tools the hopper adds to it (issue #716), its `egress` hosts when it names any (issue #1875: each `host:port` its boxes may reach through the egress proxy), its `bastionTargets` when it names any (issue #2146: each target a bastion of it may forward to), and its scope, the vault secrets its boxes may ask for, its operation profiles (issue #584) — a `terraform-workspace` profile with its state `backend` (`bucket`, `region`, `keyPrefix`; issue #715), which the read-only check probes and no approval covers —, its `probeMarks` when it has any (issue #916: a read probe of the read-only check marked `expect-denied` or `skip`), and who saved it. A scope wider than the one approved, a new image, a new egress host, or a new bastion target, waits for a person (`vault.approved`); a new profile waits for its approval (`template.profile_approved`).

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `template` | string | yes |
| `image` | string | yes |
| `tools` | string[] | no |
| `egress` | string[] | no |
| `bastionTargets` | string[] | no |
| `secrets` | string[] | yes |
| `profiles` | object[] | no |
| `probeMarks` | object | no |
| `by` | string | yes |

```json
{
  "template": "kube",
  "image": "localhost/box-kubectl:1",
  "secrets": [
    "KUBE_TOKEN"
  ],
  "profiles": [
    {
      "operation": "read",
      "asset": {
        "kind": "cluster",
        "name": "lab"
      }
    }
  ],
  "by": "Ada"
}
```

## `template.removed`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/template.removed.v1.json`). A template was removed (issue #558): only when no box of it was attached (issue #604); its access approvals are revoked.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `template` | string | yes |
| `by` | string | yes |

```json
{
  "template": "kube",
  "by": "Ada"
}
```

## `vault.approved`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/vault.approved.v1.json`). A person approved a template as it is (issue #558): its image (with its tools, issue #716), its egress hosts (issue #1875), its bastion targets (issue #2146) and its whole scope. From then on its boxes take jobs (issue #602) and may be given those vault secrets, and only those. Its read profiles are approved with it (`template.profile_approved`); a write, sync or apply profile is not. `by`: a person, or for a template made for a job `the read policy`, `the auto-approve policy` (issue #1001), `a remembered write approval` (issue #1001) or `skip template approval`. `jobs` (issue #2197 part 3): a run card approved with no allow again approves those jobs' runs only; absent, every job's.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `template` | string | yes |
| `image` | string | yes |
| `tools` | string[] | no |
| `egress` | string[] | no |
| `bastionTargets` | string[] | no |
| `secrets` | string[] | yes |
| `by` | string | yes |
| `jobs` | string[] | no |

```json
{
  "template": "kube",
  "image": "localhost/box-kubectl:1",
  "secrets": [
    "KUBE_TOKEN"
  ],
  "by": "Ada"
}
```

## `vault.revoked`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/vault.revoked.v1.json`). A person revoked a template's approval (issue #602). Its boxes take no new job, and are given no vault secret, until a person approves it again (`vault.approved`). Every access approval of its operation profiles is revoked with it.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `template` | string | yes |
| `by` | string | yes |

```json
{
  "template": "kube",
  "by": "Ada"
}
```

## `template.profile_approved`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/template.profile_approved.v1.json`). An operation profile of a template was approved in access (issue #584): with the template for a read profile (level low), or by its own explicit approval for a write, sync or apply profile (level high). Access then allows the template's jobs that operation on that asset.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `template` | string | yes |
| `operation` | `read` \| `write` \| `sync` \| `apply` \| `observe` | yes |
| `asset` | object | yes |
| `level` | `low` \| `medium` \| `high` | yes |
| `by` | string | yes |

```json
{
  "template": "kube",
  "operation": "write",
  "asset": {
    "kind": "cluster",
    "name": "lab"
  },
  "level": "high",
  "by": "Ada"
}
```

## `template.checked`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/template.checked.v1.json`). The read-only check of a template ended (issue #716): `passed`, or `failed` with the probes that failed and any problem. A probe the check did not run (`not-run`, issue #715: a workspace need with no state backend) is a failed probe: unproven, never passed. A template a job asked for with read needs only, or read and observe needs (issue #2146), takes no box and no job until the check of its current version passed. `artifact` (issue #715): the artifact that holds its report, of the job that asked for the template; absent when no job did.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `template` | string | yes |
| `state` | `passed` \| `failed` | yes |
| `failed` | string[] | yes |
| `problem` | string | no |
| `artifact` | string | no |

```json
{
  "template": "asked-3f9a1c2b7d10",
  "state": "failed",
  "failed": [
    "aws.iam-create-user on 123456789012 (allowed)"
  ],
  "artifact": "0b6f7c1e-5d2a-4c8e-9f31-7a2d4e6b8c90"
}
```

## `template.check_requested`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/template.check_requested.v1.json`). A person asked for the read-only check of a template to run again (issue #716), or (issue #1779) a minting credential was set for the account or cluster of a read need its failed check got no credential for (`by` `minting credential <name>`): its last check is dropped, and the next check pass runs one.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `template` | string | yes |
| `by` | string | yes |

```json
{
  "template": "asked-3f9a1c2b7d10",
  "by": "Ada"
}
```

## `vault.delivered`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/vault.delivered.v1.json`). A vault secret was delivered to a box, for a job at work on it (issue #558): sealed to the box client's own request, never in an environment or a file. The secret's name, the template, the machine and the job; never the value. `backend`: the vault backend it was read from at that moment (issue #585), when it is kept in one.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | yes |
| `template` | string | yes |
| `machine` | string | yes |
| `job` | string | yes |
| `backend` | string | no |

```json
{
  "name": "KUBE_TOKEN",
  "template": "kube",
  "machine": "hopper-sandbox-kube",
  "job": "f3b1c2d4-0000-4000-8000-000000000001"
}
```

## `vault.refused`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/vault.refused.v1.json`). A box asked for a vault secret and was refused (issue #558): a template not approved for it, a machine of no template, a job not at work there, a token the hopper did not give, a vault backend that is gone or cannot read it (`backend`, issue #585). Or a launch's agent credential was refused (issue #708, part 10): its template is not approved for it, or its value is no Claude token; then `machine` is the box that was not started, and there is no `job`. `reason` says which; never a value.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | yes |
| `machine` | string | yes |
| `template` | string | no |
| `job` | string | no |
| `backend` | string | no |
| `reason` | string | yes |

```json
{
  "name": "PROD_KEY",
  "machine": "hopper-sandbox-kube",
  "template": "kube",
  "job": "f3b1c2d4-0000-4000-8000-000000000001",
  "reason": "kube is not approved for PROD_KEY: a person adds it to the template and approves it"
}
```

## `vault.minted`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/vault.minted.v1.json`). The vault minted a short-lived credential for a job on a box (issue #580): an AWS role session (`aws`) or a Kubernetes token (`kube`) for the operation on the asset, from the minting credential named, after Access allowed it. `decision` is the id of Access's decision (Settings → Access); `renewal` when the job had one for that profile before. `plan` (issue #870): the approved, current plan an operation that changes infrastructure named. `principal` (issue #871): who the credential writes as, as an audit log names it (the assumed role's session, the service account), so a write it made while valid is not out of band. `bound` (issue #1371): the Secret a need box's Kubernetes token is bound to; deleting it (`vault.unbound`) ends the token. `actions` (issue #2206): the granted AWS actions, each on its resource, a need step's session was narrowed to. A mint that names a plan and is no renewal is an apply: the notifiers send it as `infra.plan_applied`, with the watchers of the plan's environments (issue #870 part 4). Never the credential.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `kind` | `aws` \| `kube` | yes |
| `operation` | `read` \| `write` \| `sync` \| `apply` \| `observe` | yes |
| `asset` | object | yes |
| `template` | string | yes |
| `machine` | string | yes |
| `job` | string | yes |
| `credential` | string | yes |
| `decision` | string | yes |
| `expiresAt` | string | yes |
| `renewal` | boolean | yes |
| `plan` | string | no |
| `principal` | string | no |
| `bound` | object | no |
| `actions` | object[] | no |

```json
{
  "kind": "kube",
  "operation": "read",
  "asset": {
    "kind": "namespace",
    "name": "lab/web"
  },
  "template": "kube",
  "machine": "hopper-sandbox-kube",
  "job": "f3b1c2d4-0000-4000-8000-000000000001",
  "credential": "KUBE_LAB",
  "decision": "6c1d2e3f-0000-4000-8000-000000000002",
  "expiresAt": "2026-10-09T12:10:00.000Z",
  "renewal": false,
  "principal": "system:serviceaccount:web:hopper-read",
  "bound": {
    "namespace": "web",
    "secret": "hopper-mint-0b1c2d3e-0000-4000-8000-000000000004"
  }
}
```

## `vault.mint_refused`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/vault.mint_refused.v1.json`). A box asked the vault to mint a credential and got none (issue #580): Access denied it — the profile waits at the first-time gate on Settings → Vault, or the template does not declare it —, or no minting credential covers the asset, or the outside service refused. `decision` when Access answered; never a value.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `mint` | object | yes |
| `machine` | string | yes |
| `template` | string | no |
| `job` | string | no |
| `reason` | string | yes |
| `decision` | string | no |

```json
{
  "mint": {
    "kind": "kube",
    "operation": "write",
    "asset": {
      "kind": "namespace",
      "name": "lab/web"
    }
  },
  "machine": "hopper-sandbox-kube",
  "template": "kube",
  "job": "f3b1c2d4-0000-4000-8000-000000000001",
  "reason": "Access denied it: template kube is not approved to write on namespace lab/web. write on namespace lab/web waits for a person's approval on Access requests (the first-time gate)",
  "decision": "6c1d2e3f-0000-4000-8000-000000000003"
}
```

## `vault.mint_tested`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/vault.mint_tested.v1.json`). A person tested a minting credential (issue #781, `hopper vault mint-test`): the vault minted a read session for the `aws-role`, as for a job, and asked STS who it is; or (issue #854) a read token for the `cluster`, and asked the cluster who it is and which namespaces it lists. `arn` is the role the session assumed, with `sessionName`; `user` is who the cluster says the token is, with `sessionName` when it signed in through EKS; `roleArn` and `account` the role a session or an EKS token signed in as (issue #1766), and `credential` the minting credential the test used — for a cluster found in the AWS accounts, the AWS one it was found with; `reason` when nothing was minted or STS or the cluster refused. Never a key or a token.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `asset` | object \| string | yes |
| `credential` | string | no |
| `roleArn` | string | no |
| `account` | string | no |
| `sessionName` | string | no |
| `arn` | string | no |
| `user` | string | no |
| `expiresAt` | string | no |
| `reason` | string | no |
| `by` | string | yes |

```json
{
  "asset": {
    "kind": "aws-role",
    "name": "123456789012/diag"
  },
  "credential": "AWS_LAB",
  "sessionName": "hopper-mint-test",
  "arn": "arn:aws:sts::123456789012:assumed-role/diag/hopper-mint-test",
  "expiresAt": "2026-10-09T12:15:00.000Z",
  "by": "Ada"
}
```

## `vault.discovery_minted`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/vault.discovery_minted.v1.json`). Topology discovery (issue #1781 part 3, design.md "The infrastructure topology") asked the vault for a read credential: a read session of an account's read role (`aws-role/<account>/hopper-read`), or a read token for a `cluster`. `credential`: the minting credential it came from (for a cluster found in the AWS accounts, the AWS one); `expiresAt` when it was minted; `reason` when nothing was minted. Never a key or a token. On no job's timeline.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `asset` | object | yes |
| `credential` | string | no |
| `expiresAt` | string | no |
| `reason` | string | no |

```json
{
  "asset": {
    "kind": "aws-role",
    "name": "123456789012/hopper-read"
  },
  "credential": "AWS_LAB",
  "expiresAt": "2026-10-17T12:15:00.000Z"
}
```

## `vault.check_minted`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/vault.check_minted.v1.json`). The vault minted a short-lived read credential for a read-only check box of a template (issue #797): an AWS role session (`aws`) or a Kubernetes token (`kube`) for the read need on the asset, from the minting credential named, after Access allowed the template it (`decision`, a decision of the check on Settings → Access). The check runs no job; `check` is its check box. `bound` (issue #1371): the Secret a Kubernetes token is bound to, deleted when the check box ends (`vault.unbound`). Never the credential.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `kind` | `aws` \| `kube` | yes |
| `operation` | `read` \| `write` \| `sync` \| `apply` \| `observe` | yes |
| `asset` | object | yes |
| `template` | string | yes |
| `check` | string | yes |
| `credential` | string | yes |
| `decision` | string | yes |
| `expiresAt` | string | yes |
| `bound` | object | no |

```json
{
  "kind": "aws",
  "operation": "read",
  "asset": {
    "kind": "aws-role",
    "name": "123456789012/readonly"
  },
  "template": "asked-0afb8cc6",
  "check": "hopper-check-asked-0afb8cc6-mgk2x0",
  "credential": "AWS_LAB",
  "decision": "6c1d2e3f-0000-4000-8000-000000000004",
  "expiresAt": "2026-10-11T12:15:00.000Z"
}
```

## `vault.check_mint_refused`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/vault.check_mint_refused.v1.json`). A read-only check box of a template got no read credential for one read need (issue #797), and the check failed with the reason: the vault mints for none of the asset's kind (`mint.kind` absent), Access denied it, no minting credential covers the asset, or the outside service refused. `decision` when Access answered; never a value.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `mint` | object | yes |
| `template` | string | yes |
| `check` | string | yes |
| `reason` | string | yes |
| `decision` | string | no |

```json
{
  "mint": {
    "kind": "kube",
    "operation": "read",
    "asset": {
      "kind": "cluster",
      "name": "lab"
    }
  },
  "template": "asked-0afb8cc6",
  "check": "hopper-check-asked-0afb8cc6-mgk2x0",
  "reason": "no minting credential mints for cluster lab: a person adds one on Settings → Vault",
  "decision": "6c1d2e3f-0000-4000-8000-000000000005"
}
```

## `vault.binding_named`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/vault.binding_named.v1.json`). The vault named the Secret a sandbox's Kubernetes token is to be bound to (issue #1628), before it asked the minting credential for the token: the minter makes that Secret. `box` is the need box or check box, `job` the job it served (none for a check box), `credential` the minting credential. A hopper that stopped before the mint's own event (`vault.minted`, `vault.check_minted`) still knows the Secret: the reconcile pass deletes it (`vault.unbound`) once no sandbox holds it. Never the token.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `box` | string | yes |
| `job` | string | no |
| `credential` | string | yes |
| `namespace` | string | yes |
| `secret` | string | yes |

```json
{
  "box": "hopper-need-kube-1a2b3c4d",
  "job": "f3b1c2d4-0000-4000-8000-000000000001",
  "credential": "KUBE_LAB",
  "namespace": "web",
  "secret": "hopper-mint-0b1c2d3e-0000-4000-8000-000000000004"
}
```

## `vault.unbound`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/vault.unbound.v1.json`). A sandbox ended, and the Secret its Kubernetes token was bound to was deleted (issue #1371): the API server refuses that token at once. `box` is the need box or check box, `job` the job it served (none for a check box), `credential` the minting credential that made the token. Its end does it, whatever the outcome; the reconcile pass, at start and every 5 minutes, does it for a binding a hopper that stopped, or an unbind that failed, left. Never the token.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `box` | string | yes |
| `job` | string | no |
| `credential` | string | yes |
| `namespace` | string | yes |
| `secret` | string | yes |

```json
{
  "box": "hopper-need-kube-1a2b3c4d",
  "job": "f3b1c2d4-0000-4000-8000-000000000001",
  "credential": "KUBE_LAB",
  "namespace": "web",
  "secret": "hopper-mint-0b1c2d3e-0000-4000-8000-000000000004"
}
```

## `bastion.started`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/bastion.started.v1.json`). A job started a bastion (issue #2146, design.md "Bastions"): one need box of `template` that holds `kubectl port-forward` to each of `targets` (`<cluster>/<namespace>/<kind>/<name>:<port>`) on 127.0.0.1 inside it, its kube tokens minted for its observe profiles (each a `vault.minted` with `box` as its machine) and minted again while it runs, and, part 6, the vault `secrets` it holds for bastion reads, by name (each a `vault.step_delivered` with `box` as its host). It ends at `expiresAt` unless it is used before. Never a token or a value.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `bastion` | string | yes |
| `template` | string | yes |
| `box` | string | yes |
| `targets` | string[] | yes |
| `secrets` | string[] | no |
| `expiresAt` | string | yes |

```json
{
  "bastion": "5c1d2e3f-0000-4000-8000-000000000001",
  "template": "observe-uat",
  "box": "hopper-bastion-observe-uat-5c1d2e3f",
  "targets": [
    "uat/monitoring/svc/prometheus-server:9090"
  ],
  "expiresAt": "2026-10-20T13:00:00.000Z"
}
```

## `bastion.ended`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/bastion.ended.v1.json`). A bastion ended (issue #2146): `reason` `stopped` (by the job, a person or the hopper, `by`), `expired` (its TTL passed with no use), `job-ended`, or `failed` (a renewal was refused, or its box ended by itself: `problem`). Its tokens are released and its box burned.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `bastion` | string | yes |
| `template` | string | yes |
| `box` | string | yes |
| `reason` | `stopped` \| `expired` \| `job-ended` \| `failed` | yes |
| `by` | string | no |
| `problem` | string | no |

```json
{
  "bastion": "5c1d2e3f-0000-4000-8000-000000000001",
  "template": "observe-uat",
  "box": "hopper-bastion-observe-uat-5c1d2e3f",
  "reason": "stopped",
  "by": "job"
}
```

## `bastion.relayed`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/bastion.relayed.v1.json`). A job's relay connection to `target` of its bastion ended (issue #2146 part 3, design.md "Bastions"): Access allowed it (`bastion#can_relay`, the target approved with the bastion's template), it opened at `openedAt` and was open `ms` milliseconds. Never what went through it.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `bastion` | string | yes |
| `target` | string | yes |
| `openedAt` | string | yes |
| `ms` | integer | yes |

```json
{
  "bastion": "5c1d2e3f-0000-4000-8000-000000000001",
  "target": "uat/monitoring/svc/prometheus-server:9090",
  "openedAt": "2026-10-20T12:10:00.000Z",
  "ms": 1500
}
```

## `bastion.relay_refused`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/bastion.relay_refused.v1.json`). A job's relay connection to `target` of its bastion was refused (issue #2146 part 3): Access denied it, or could not be asked (`reason`); no command started in the box.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `bastion` | string | yes |
| `target` | string | yes |
| `reason` | string | yes |

```json
{
  "bastion": "5c1d2e3f-0000-4000-8000-000000000001",
  "target": "uat/monitoring/svc/grafana:80",
  "reason": "job:u1/j1 may not relay to uat/monitoring/svc/grafana:80"
}
```

## `bastion.read`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/bastion.read.v1.json`). A bastion read ran (issue #2146 part 6, design.md "Bastions"): one HTTP `method` (GET, or a POST to Grafana's data source query) of `path` on `target`, run with curl in the bastion's box over a relay connection Access allowed, with a vault secret's header from its file there when the job named one. `status` and `bytes`: the target's answer; `problem`: why there was none (curl's words, or an answer over 2 MiB). `ms`: how long it took. Never the secret or the answer.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `bastion` | string | yes |
| `target` | string | yes |
| `method` | `GET` \| `POST` | yes |
| `path` | string | yes |
| `status` | integer | no |
| `bytes` | integer | no |
| `problem` | string | no |
| `ms` | integer | yes |

```json
{
  "bastion": "5c1d2e3f-0000-4000-8000-000000000001",
  "target": "uat/monitoring/svc/grafana:80",
  "method": "GET",
  "path": "/api/search?query=latency",
  "status": 200,
  "bytes": 512,
  "ms": 120
}
```

The skill, the template, the machine, the job, and what the job said it needs it for. Once per job and request.

## `vault.credential_given`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/vault.credential_given.v1.json`). A person gave a credential for a credential request (issue #583): a vault secret, added to the template's scope. The secret's name, the template and the box; never the value. `backend`: the vault backend it was read from, when it is kept in one.

## `vault.read_policy_set`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/vault.read_policy_set.v1.json`). An admin set the read policy (issue #716): the assets the hopper approves read on with no person, for a template a job asks for (`sandbox-template`, `sandbox`). The read policy never approves write, sync or apply: only skip template approval does (issue #991). Empty: the read policy approves nothing.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `assets` | string[] | yes |
| `by` | string | yes |

```json
{
  "assets": [
    "cluster/lab",
    "aws-account/*"
  ],
  "by": "Ada"
}
```

## `vault.sandbox_approvals_set`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/vault.sandbox_approvals_set.v1.json`). An admin set the sandbox approval toggles (issue #991): `skipTemplateApproval`, a template the hopper makes for a job is approved at once, its write, sync and apply profiles with it; `skipSandboxApproval`, a box a job asks for starts at once, a high-blast-radius one too. Both on is sandbox YOLO. `autoApprove` (issue #1001): the blast radius levels whose templates and runs are approved with no person. `rememberWritesHours` (issue #1001): how long a person's write, sync or apply approval is remembered; 0, until an admin forgets it. Issue #1472: `standingReadGrant`, the standing read grant: a job on a box of a template that only reads what the read policy holds gets the vault grant with no person.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `skipTemplateApproval` | boolean | yes |
| `skipSandboxApproval` | boolean | yes |
| `autoApprove` | object | no |
| `rememberWritesHours` | integer | no |
| `standingReadGrant` | boolean | no |
| `by` | string | yes |

```json
{
  "skipTemplateApproval": true,
  "skipSandboxApproval": true,
  "autoApprove": {
    "low": true,
    "medium": false,
    "high": false
  },
  "by": "Ada"
}
```

## `sandbox.strictness_changed`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/sandbox.strictness_changed.v1.json`). An admin changed the sandbox strictness in Settings → Vault (issue #655, brake 2): which sandbox runs gate 2 may approve with no person, `default`, by blast radius level (`radius`) and by template (`templates`). `relaxed` and `standard`: the approval toggles and policies decide; `strict`: a person approves each run of a medium or high radius template, or one with no rating; `locked`: a person approves each run. It applies at once. `from` and `to`, `by` who changed it.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `from` | object | yes |
| `to` | object | yes |
| `by` | string | yes |

```json
{
  "from": {
    "default": "standard",
    "radius": {},
    "templates": {}
  },
  "to": {
    "default": "standard",
    "radius": {
      "high": "strict"
    },
    "templates": {
      "aws-prod": "locked"
    }
  },
  "by": "Ada"
}
```

## `vault.sandbox_requested`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/vault.sandbox_requested.v1.json`). A running job asked the hopper for a box of a template (issue #991, `sh "$HOPPER_SKILL" sandbox --needs …`, or `--template NAME`, issue #1471), or the hopper asked for one before the job started, as the job's prompt names the template (issue #1471): the sandbox request `request`, kept in memory. It waits for a person on Access requests unless skip sandbox approval is on. On the job's timeline.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `request` | string | yes |
| `template` | string | yes |

```json
{
  "request": "b2c1",
  "template": "asked-3f2a9c1d0e4b"
}
```

## `vault.run_card_opened`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/vault.run_card_opened.v1.json`). A new **run card** (issue #2197, design.md "One approval per sandbox run"): the job's run of `template`, or its ask that waits on it, waits for a person on Access requests. `waits` says what the one approval approves: the template (its image, tools, egress, secrets or profiles), the run, or both. `purpose`: why the job asks, in its words. One per job and template while the hopper runs; not while Jev reads the run. The notifiers send it (the Grok Bot routine as `vault.run_card_opened`, with the job's priority and the Access requests link). On the job's timeline.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `template` | string | yes |
| `waits` | object | yes |
| `purpose` | string | no |

```json
{
  "template": "asked-3f2a9c1d0e4b",
  "waits": {
    "template": true,
    "run": true
  },
  "purpose": "Rotate the deploy key of the staging cluster"
}
```

## `vault.sandbox_approved`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/vault.sandbox_approved.v1.json`). A sandbox request was approved (issue #991): `by` a person, `skip sandbox approval` when the toggle approved it, `the auto-approve policy` with the template's `radius` (issue #1001), `the template's approval by <person>` when a person approved the template this job asked for, or `a remembered write approval` (issue #1001) when a person approved each change the template makes before, or `Jev` when Jev's sandbox check (issue #655 part 13, the decision point `sandbox-request` active) allowed a run one of those would approve. It starts no box (issue #1349): the job's box steps then run, each in a sandbox of its own, burned after it. On the job's timeline.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `request` | string | yes |
| `template` | string | yes |
| `by` | string | yes |
| `radius` | `low` \| `medium` \| `high` | no |

```json
{
  "request": "b2c1",
  "template": "asked-3f2a9c1d0e4b",
  "by": "skip sandbox approval"
}
```

## `vault.sandbox_declined`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/vault.sandbox_declined.v1.json`). A person declined a sandbox request (issue #991), with the `reason` the job is told. No box starts. On the job's timeline. Issue #655 part 9: `by` is `the hold timeout` when no person answered it within 24 hours; that deny is of this request only, and lowers no trust. Part 13: `by` is `Jev` when Jev's sandbox check (the decision point `sandbox-request` active) denied it, with its reason: a deny at gate 2, which lowers the job's trust as a person's does (`job.trust_lowered`, `job.quarantined`). Part 16: `by` is `the minimum trust` when the template has an operation profile whose minimum trust the job's stamp does not meet: declined at once, by policy, before Jev or a person; the job's trust stays.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `request` | string | yes |
| `template` | string | yes |
| `reason` | string | yes |
| `by` | string | yes |

```json
{
  "request": "b2c1",
  "template": "asked-3f2a9c1d0e4b",
  "reason": "not this week",
  "by": "Ada"
}
```

## `vault.sandbox_started`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/vault.sandbox_started.v1.json`). The box of a sandbox request started (issue #991): `container`, the sandbox box, which joined as a machine. Recorded until issue #1349; an approval now starts no box. On the job's timeline.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `request` | string | yes |
| `template` | string | yes |
| `container` | string | yes |

```json
{
  "request": "b2c1",
  "template": "asked-3f2a9c1d0e4b",
  "container": "hopper-sandbox-asked-3f2a9c1d0e4b-1"
}
```

## `vault.sandbox_failed`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/vault.sandbox_failed.v1.json`). The box of an approved sandbox request did not start (issue #991): `reason`. Recorded until issue #1349; an approval now starts no box. On the job's timeline.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `request` | string | yes |
| `template` | string | yes |
| `reason` | string | yes |

```json
{
  "request": "b2c1",
  "template": "asked-3f2a9c1d0e4b",
  "reason": "the start check did not pass in 30 s"
}
```

## `vault.write_forgotten`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/vault.write_forgotten.v1.json`). An admin forgot a remembered write approval (issue #1001): the `operation` on the `asset` a person approved before. A later template or sandbox run that changes it waits for a person again.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `operation` | `write` \| `sync` \| `apply` \| `observe` | yes |
| `asset` | object | yes |
| `by` | string | yes |

## `vault.grant_asked`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/vault.grant_asked.v1.json`). A job on a box asked the vault for a secret or a minted credential, or a job's Windows sandbox step asked for a vault secret (issue #731), or its box step (issue #1875), and its item has no vault grant (issue #652): it was refused, and the hopper asked a person to grant it the vault (Settings → Vault). The job, its item's key, the machine and the template (a box), the `windowsHost` (a Windows step), or the need `box` and the template (a box step), and the first thing it asked for (a secret's name, or `<kind> <operation> <asset>`). Once per job.

| `key` | string | yes |
| `machine` | string | no |
| `template` | string | no |

| `box` | string | no |
| `name` | string | yes |

```json

  "job": "f3b1c2d4-0000-4000-8000-000000000001",
  "key": "https://github.com/octo-org/hello/issues/7",
  "machine": "hopper-sandbox-web",
  "template": "web",
  "name": "KUBE_TOKEN"
}
```

## `vault.granted`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/vault.granted.v1.json`). A person granted a job's item the vault (issue #652), after Access allowed it (OpenFGA `vault_grant#can_grant`) — on Settings → Vault, or as the submitter of a direct job that authorizes `vault` (issue #901): its jobs — this one, and those Run again or Rework make — get what their box's template gives. `by` who granted it; a delegate approver's (issue #1138) names the delegate and the person it acts for; `standing read grant` (issue #1472) when the user's standing read grant gave it, with no person, to a job on a box of a template that only reads what the read policy holds.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `job` | string | yes |
| `key` | string | yes |
| `by` | string | yes |

```json
{
  "job": "f3b1c2d4-0000-4000-8000-000000000001",
  "key": "https://github.com/octo-org/hello/issues/7",
  "by": "octocat"
}
```

## `vault.grant_revoked`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/vault.grant_revoked.v1.json`). A person took back a job's item's vault grant (issue #652): its jobs get nothing from the vault again until a person grants it again. `by` who took it back. A quarantine of the job takes it back too (issue #655 part 6): `by` `quarantine by <person>`.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `job` | string | yes |
| `key` | string | yes |
| `by` | string | yes |

{
  "job": "f3b1c2d4-0000-4000-8000-000000000001",
