```json
  "by": "octocat"
}
```

## `vault.grant_denied`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/vault.grant_denied.v1.json`). A person, or a delegate approver for them (issue #1138), denied a job's vault grant ask: the ask goes, and the job, which still has no vault grant, asks no more. `by` who denied it; a delegate's `by` names the delegate and the person it acts for.

```json
  "job": "f3b1c2d4-0000-4000-8000-000000000001",
```


## `vault.action_revoked`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/vault.action_revoked.v1.json`). A person revoked an action grant (issue #2206): the next ask of that role, action and resource waits for a person again; a credential minted before keeps its 15 minutes. `by` who revoked it.

| `role` | string | yes |
| `action` | string | yes |
| `resource` | string | yes |
| `by` | string | yes |

```json
{
  "role": "167028478405/hopper-action",
  "action": "eks:UpdateNodegroupConfig",
  "resource": "arn:aws:eks:us-west-1:167028478405:nodegroup/identity-eks/identity-eks-nodes/*",
  "by": "octocat"
}
```

## `yolo_mode.changed`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/yolo_mode.changed.v1.json`). An admin changed yolo mode (issue #579): whether jobs may merge their own pull requests once the repo's checks pass — `on` for every job repository, `repos` per repository (`owner/repo`, lowercased), which wins. `changeKinds` (issue #1076): the change-kind rules over the built-in rule, `default` and per repository, and the merge gate of each kind. `push` (issue #1806): direct push's repositories, where a job may push straight to the target branch as a fast-forward; absent: none. `from` and `to` the settings, `by` who changed them. Done never depends on it.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `from` | object | yes |
| `to` | object | yes |
| `by` | string | yes |

```json
{
  "from": {
    "on": false,
    "repos": {}
  },
  "to": {
    "on": false,
    "repos": {
      "owner/repo": true
    }
  },
  "by": "owner"
}
```

## `job.pull_request_merged`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/job.pull_request_merged.v1.json`). A finished job's pull request, followed after its end (issue #579), was merged: its item is done (`hopper:done` on GitHub). `part`: it shipped part of the item, and the next part may now be taken; a merge that did not close the item is a part (issue #721), and a merge recorded as the whole item before issue #721 that did not close it is recorded again, once, as a part. A part that makes every part the item declares done marks the item done (issue #729). `byHopper`: the hopper merged it itself (yolo mode on for its repository, issue #637). `person`, `via`: a person pressed Merge now (issue #677), in the UI or the operator CLI. `stray` (issue #1420): no job followed it — a job named it, and no job of its item worked on it — and it was merged on GitHub; it moves no work item, only marks its own pull request merged.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `pullRequest` | string | yes |
| `part` | boolean | yes |
| `byHopper` | boolean | no |
| `stray` | boolean | no |
| `person` | string | no |
| `via` | `ui` \| `cli` \| `api` | no |

```json
{
  "pullRequest": "https://github.com/owner/repo/pull/12",
  "part": false
}
```

## `job.pull_request_closed`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/job.pull_request_closed.v1.json`). A finished job's pull request, followed after its end (issue #579), was closed without a merge: its item is flagged (`hopper:pr-closed` on GitHub) until a person acts. `part`: it shipped part of the item. `person`, `via`: a person pressed Close PR (issue #677), in the UI or the operator CLI. `superseded` (issue #1143): the hopper closed it itself, as nothing was left to land, and why: its issue was closed as completed by another pull request (the item is done, `hopper:done`), or its base branch already has every commit of it. `stray` (issue #1143 part 4): no job followed it — a job named it, and no job of its item worked on it —; the close ends no wait of its item. A stray closed on GitHub, with no `superseded`, is recorded too (issue #1420).

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `pullRequest` | string | yes |
| `part` | boolean | yes |
| `superseded` | string | no |
| `stray` | boolean | no |
| `person` | string | no |
| `via` | `ui` \| `cli` \| `api` | no |

```json
{
  "pullRequest": "https://github.com/owner/repo/pull/13",
  "part": true
}
```

## `job.pull_request_abandoned`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/job.pull_request_abandoned.v1.json`). A finished job's item was closed as not planned on GitHub while its pull request, followed after its end, was still open (issue #428): the job is abandoned upstream. The hopper follows the pull request no more and never merges it, and leaves it open; `hopper:pr-ready` comes off and no end label goes on. A reopened issue with that pull request still open is followed again. `part`: it shipped part of the item.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `pullRequest` | string | yes |
| `part` | boolean | yes |

```json
{
  "pullRequest": "https://github.com/owner/repo/pull/13",
  "part": false
}
```

## `job.finish_briefed`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/job.finish_briefed.v1.json`). A job that ended done left its own pull request with merge conflicts, failing checks or as a draft (issues #626, #736): one fixed step finishes it, so the job goes on in its own session with that step's fixed brief, in place of a failure and a hand-off. `step`: `rebase` (onto its base branch; merge conflicts come first), `fix_checks` (its failing checks, issue #736) or `mark_ready` (a draft, marked ready for review). At most three per run; then the job is judged as any other.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `pullRequest` | string | yes |
| `step` | `rebase` \| `fix_checks` \| `mark_ready` | yes |

```json
{
  "pullRequest": "https://github.com/owner/repo/pull/14",
  "step": "rebase"
}
```

## `job.checks_rerun`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/job.checks_rerun.v1.json`). A job ended done while the checks of its own pull request were red (issue #1230, the cause Own PR checks red): before it is sent back to fix them, the hopper ran its failed checks again once, the flake guard, once for each head commit. `recordId`: its failure record. `pullRequest`, `head`: the pull request and its head commit. `checks`: the checks run again, by name; none when none could be. `refused`: why a check was not run again (no GitHub Actions job, no Actions write permission). Red again, the job goes on to fix them (`job.continued`).

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `recordId` | string | yes |
| `pullRequest` | string | yes |
| `head` | string | yes |
| `checks` | string[] | yes |
| `refused` | string | no |

```json
{
  "recordId": "f-1",
  "pullRequest": "https://github.com/owner/repo/pull/14",
  "head": "4e4e68e4",
  "checks": [
    "test (node 24)"
  ]
}
```

## `job.checks_rerun_asked`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/job.checks_rerun_asked.v1.json`). The hopper asks GitHub to run the failed checks of a job's own pull request again (issue #1607): recorded before it asks, so a stop while it asks makes no second run again of the same head commit. Fields as `job.checks_rerun`; `checks`, the checks it asks to run again. With no `job.checks_rerun` after it, the hopper stopped meanwhile: whether any check ran again is not known, so the job may run them again itself.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `recordId` | string | yes |
| `pullRequest` | string | yes |
| `head` | string | yes |
| `checks` | string[] | yes |

```json
{
  "recordId": "f-1",
  "pullRequest": "https://github.com/owner/repo/pull/14",
  "head": "4e4e68e4",
  "checks": [
    "test (node 24)"
  ]
}
```

## `job.pull_request_tended`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/job.pull_request_tended.v1.json`). A PR waiting job's pull request got merge conflicts with its base branch, or failing checks, while it waited (issue #736): the hopper ran its item again (`job.rerun`, by `tending`) with the tend brief, so a new job brings the same pull request back to ready, and this job follows it no more. `step`: `rebase` or `fix_checks`. `nextJobId`: the new job. A rebase is never capped (issue #786); at most three `fix_checks` tends in a row of one pull request, then it waits on a person. `person`, `via`: a person pressed Tend again (issue #1010) after the hopper gave up on it, in the UI or over the API.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `pullRequest` | string | yes |
| `step` | `rebase` \| `fix_checks` | yes |
| `nextJobId` | string | yes |
| `person` | string | no |
| `via` | `ui` \| `cli` \| `api` | no |

```json
{
  "pullRequest": "https://github.com/owner/repo/pull/14",
  "step": "rebase",
  "nextJobId": "j2"
}
```

## `job.pull_request_base_merged`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/job.pull_request_base_merged.v1.json`). A PR waiting job's pull request had merge conflicts with its base branch, and the hopper merged the base branch into it in its own mirror and pushed the merge commit to its branch (issue #967): no job, no lane. `commit`: the merge commit. `resolved`: the Markdown files whose conflict it resolved by keeping the lines both sides added, the base branch's first. The job still follows the pull request; its checks run again. A conflict it does not resolve goes to a tend job (`job.pull_request_tended`).

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `pullRequest` | string | yes |
| `commit` | string | yes |
| `resolved` | string[] | yes |

```json
{
  "pullRequest": "https://github.com/owner/repo/pull/14",
  "commit": "4b825dc642cb6eb9a060e54bf8d69288fbee4904",
  "resolved": [
    "WHATS-NEW.md"
  ]
}
```

## `job.pull_request_retargeted`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/job.pull_request_retargeted.v1.json`). A followed job's open pull request had a base branch that is not its repository's landing branch (its landing batch setting, never GitHub's default branch) and is no open pull request's head: the hopper changed its base to the landing branch (issue #1143), with no job, and said so in one comment on it. `from`: the base before; `to`: the landing branch. `stray` (issue #1143 part 4): no job followed it — a job named it, and no job of its item worked on it.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `pullRequest` | string | yes |
| `from` | string | yes |
| `to` | string | yes |
| `stray` | boolean | no |

```json
{
  "pullRequest": "https://github.com/owner/repo/pull/15",
  "from": "dev",
  "to": "main"
}
```

## `job.pull_request_followed`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/job.pull_request_followed.v1.json`). A done job — or a failed one that is no failed tend, issue #786 — that followed no pull request — it ended before the hopper followed pull requests, or its follow ended — is the newest job of its item, and its item is open, or closed as completed with an open pull request that closes it by keyword or ships part of it (issue #786), and has an open pull request on its source (issue #763): the sync loop reconciled it, and the job follows that pull request from now on, as PR waiting. It shows on the Pull requests list, and yolo mode merges it and tending tends it as any followed one. `part`: it ships part of the item ("Part of #N").

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `pullRequest` | string | yes |
| `part` | boolean | yes |

```json
{
  "pullRequest": "https://github.com/owner/repo/pull/14",
  "part": false
}
```

## `job.pull_request_seen`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/job.pull_request_seen.v1.json`). The follow saw what a followed pull request waits on change (issue #1067, part 3): `wait` is `draft` (to be marked ready), `conflicts` (a fix of its merge conflicts), `fixing_checks` (a fix of its failed checks), `checks_running` (its checks to pass) or `merge` (the merge). Recorded only when it differs from what the work-item ledger holds for the pull request; its work item waits on it.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `pullRequest` | string | yes |
| `wait` | `draft` \| `conflicts` \| `fixing_checks` \| `checks_running` \| `merge` | yes |

```json
{
  "pullRequest": "https://github.com/owner/repo/pull/14",
  "wait": "checks_running"
}
```

## `work_item.issue_closed`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/work_item.issue_closed.v1.json`). GitHub closed the issue of a work item (issue #1067, part 3): `key` is the item's source key, `reason` why it closed (`completed`, `not_planned`, `duplicate`). `via`: a GitHub delivery said it, the ledger's fallback read of an item with no news for a while, or `landing` (issue #1232): the hopper closed it itself, as done by a pull request its batch run promoted to the tested branch while the issue stayed open. Moves the item as a read of the issue does: an item no job or person acts on is done, or dropped when not planned.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `key` | string | yes |
| `reason` | string | no |
| `via` | `delivery` \| `read` \| `landing` | yes |

```json
{
  "key": "https://github.com/owner/repo/issues/9",
  "reason": "completed",
  "via": "delivery"
}
```

## `work_item.issue_reopened`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/work_item.issue_reopened.v1.json`). GitHub reopened the issue of a work item (issue #1067, part 3): `key` is the item's source key; `via` as for `work_item.issue_closed`. The item stands where its events put it again.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `key` | string | yes |
| `via` | `delivery` \| `read` | yes |

```json
{
  "key": "https://github.com/owner/repo/issues/9",
  "via": "read"
}
```

## `work_item.reconciled`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/work_item.reconciled.v1.json`). The item reconciler corrected a work item that broke its state's promise (issue #1891, design.md "The item lifecycle"): `key` is the item's source key, `from` the state it found the item in. With `replay` (`type` and `data` of its job `jobId`'s end event, `job.finished`, `job.failed`, `job.cancelled` or `job.rejected`): the ledger had the item `queued` or `working` though that job, its newest, had ended, so the item is folded again from that end. With `cause`: the item is `blocked` — `no_pr` (in PR open past its deadline with no pull request named) or `stale` (in PR open past its deadline with no open pull request a job follows) —, and waits on a person in Failures. Moves the item only while it is still in `from`, so a second one changes nothing.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `key` | string | yes |
| `from` | `waiting_for_approval` \| `queued` \| `working` \| `needs_you` \| `waiting_outside` \| `pr_open` \| `partly_done` \| `done` \| `failed` \| `blocked` \| `dropped` | yes |
| `jobId` | string | no |
| `cause` | `stale` \| `no_pr` \| `pr_closed` | no |
| `replay` | object | no |

```json
{
  "key": "https://github.com/owner/repo/issues/9",
  "from": "pr_open",
  "cause": "no_pr"
}
```

## `work_item.dropped`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/work_item.dropped.v1.json`). A person pressed Won't do on a blocked work item in Intake (issue #1891, design.md "The item lifecycle"): `key` is the item's source key, `source` the job source that listed it, `jobId` its newest job, `cause` why it was blocked (`no_pr`, `stale`, `pr_closed`), `by` who pressed it. The item is dropped at once; its issue's blocked label goes and `hopper:rejected` comes on through the GitHub outbox, so no hopper takes it again until a person runs it again. Moves the item only while it is blocked, so a second one changes nothing.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `source` | string | yes |
| `key` | string | yes |
| `jobId` | string | no |
| `cause` | `stale` \| `no_pr` \| `pr_closed` | no |
| `by` | object | no |

```json
{
  "source": "github-account",
  "key": "https://github.com/owner/repo/issues/9",
  "jobId": "job-1",
  "cause": "pr_closed",
  "by": {
    "person": "ada",
    "via": "ui"
  }
}
```

## `work_item.person_asked`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/work_item.person_asked.v1.json`). The one notice of a blocked work item (issue #1891, design.md "The item lifecycle"): the item reconciler found it stuck work for a person (Failures' `pr_open_stale`) and asked a person once. `key` is the item's source key, `cause` why it is blocked (`no_pr`, `stale`, `pr_closed`), `jobId` its newest job, `pullRequest` the pull request it names. A notifier sends it on. The item's state stays; it is asked again only once it is blocked again, or for another cause.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `key` | string | yes |
| `cause` | `stale` \| `no_pr` \| `pr_closed` | yes |
| `jobId` | string | no |
| `pullRequest` | string | no |

```json
{
  "key": "https://github.com/owner/repo/issues/9",
  "cause": "pr_closed",
  "jobId": "job-1",
  "pullRequest": "https://github.com/owner/repo/pull/14"
}
```

## `work_item.label_edited`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/work_item.label_edited.v1.json`). A person took an end label off a work item's issue by hand on GitHub (issue #1892, design.md "The item lifecycle"): the end label its state wants (`hopper:blocked` or `hopper:pr-closed` of a blocked item, `hopper:pr-ready` or `hopper:partly-done` of an item in PR open) was on at the last discover of `source` and is gone now, with the item not moved since and no write of the hopper's own on its way. `key` is the item's source key, `jobId` its newest job, `from` the state it was in, `label` the label taken off, `means` what the edit asks for: `run_again`. The item's state stays, and it keeps the ask (`runAgainAsked`): Intake gives it no reason, so the discover runs it again; the label is not put back. The new job's `job.queued` moves it, and any move forgets the ask. A label that is not on the issue when it is first seen is never read as an edit.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `source` | string | yes |
| `key` | string | yes |
| `jobId` | string | no |
| `from` | `waiting_for_approval` \| `queued` \| `working` \| `needs_you` \| `waiting_outside` \| `pr_open` \| `partly_done` \| `done` \| `failed` \| `blocked` \| `dropped` | yes |
| `label` | string | yes |
| `means` | string | yes |

```json
{
  "source": "github-account",
  "key": "https://github.com/owner/repo/issues/9",
  "jobId": "job-1",
  "from": "blocked",
  "label": "hopper:pr-closed",
  "means": "run_again"
}
```

## `job.pull_request_classified`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/job.pull_request_classified.v1.json`). A followed pull request's change kind (issue #1076), new or changed: `kind` — `docs` (docs or comments only), `tests`, `low_risk`, `code` or `sensitive` (auth, secrets, migrations, the sandbox, CI, infra, dependencies, agent instructions, or a line a content rule matches) —, read from the files and lines it changes by the repository's change rule, and `why`: a few files and the rule each matched. The kind names its merge gate: merged when ready with no person, merged when ready only with yolo mode on, or merged only by a person. The work-item ledger keeps it on the item.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `pullRequest` | string | yes |
| `kind` | `docs` \| `tests` \| `low_risk` \| `code` \| `sensitive` | yes |
| `why` | string[] | yes |

```json
{
  "pullRequest": "https://github.com/owner/repo/pull/14",
  "kind": "docs",
  "why": [
    "README.md: docs path (**/*.md)"
  ]
}
```

The answer names the vault secrets the box may use, never a value. `version`: for a built-in library skill loaded by name (issue #1909), the version the job got, and `asset` the file of it, when it is not the entry. `repoCopy`: the repository's own copy of that skill the job said it follows (`--repo-copy`): its folder in the repository, the git `tree` and `commit` that hold it, and whether it had `changed` files.

```json
}
```

## `artifact.settings_changed`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/artifact.settings_changed.v1.json`). Settings → Artifacts changed (issue #624): the size limits per artifact and per user, the retention, whether public links work and for how long, and the link base (issue #673).

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `from` | object | yes |
| `to` | object | yes |
| `by` | string | yes |

```json
{
  "from": {
    "maxBytes": 10485760,
    "userBytes": 524288000,
    "retentionDays": 30,
    "publicLinks": true,
    "linkHours": 24,
    "linkHoursMax": 168
  },
  "to": {
    "maxBytes": 10485760,
    "userBytes": 524288000,
    "retentionDays": 30,
    "publicLinks": false,
    "linkHours": 24,
    "linkHoursMax": 168,
    "linkBase": "http://192.0.2.10:4790"
  },
  "by": "github:octocat"
}
```

## `artifact.posted`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/artifact.posted.v1.json`). A job shared an artifact with its owner, who sees it already (issue #673): its link was posted on the job's issue as the job's comment (`comment`, its URL), or could not be (`error`), or the job has no issue (`issue: false`). Also on the job's stream.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `artifact` | string | yes |
| `title` | string | yes |
| `by` | string | yes |
| `comment` | string | no |
| `error` | string | no |
| `issue` | boolean | no |

```json
{
  "artifact": "a1b2c3d4-0000-4000-8000-000000000624",
  "title": "Queue wait by hour",
  "by": "job 6f1c2a9e",
  "comment": "https://github.com/octo-org/hello/issues/7#issuecomment-1"
}
```

## `tldr.written`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/tldr.written.v1.json`). A cheap model (Claude Haiku) wrote the TL;DR of a long card (issue #569): `kind` (`question`, `research`, `handoff`; a proposal has its own TL;DR part, issue #651) and its `id`, the `text` — one or two plain sentences, no Markdown or HTML — and the `model` that wrote it. Written once per text: again only when the card's text changes (a research report's next round). The card leads with it; a notification sent before it shows the agent's own summary.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `kind` | `question` \| `research` \| `handoff` | yes |
| `id` | string | yes |
| `text` | string | yes |
| `model` | string | no |

```json
{
  "kind": "question",
  "id": "q1",
  "text": "The job asks which branch to rebase onto: dev or main.",
  "model": "claude-haiku-4-5"
}
```

## `tldr.settings_changed`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/tldr.settings_changed.v1.json`). An admin turned the TL;DR on or off (issue #569): `enabled`, `from` and `to`. Off, no TL;DR is written or shown, and notifications carry none.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `from` | object | yes |
| `to` | object | yes |
| `by` | string | yes |

```json
{
  "from": {
    "enabled": true
  },
  "to": {
    "enabled": false
  },
  "by": "admin"
}
```

## `artifact.revised`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/artifact.revised.v1.json`). An artifact has a new latest revision (issue #675): a job put a file to it (`by` the job), or a person restored an older revision (`restoredFrom`), which is copied, not moved; or a person revised it with a file or another artifact's latest content (`copiedFrom`), or merged another artifact into it, whose revisions are added oldest first, each still `by` the job that made it (`mergedFrom`, issue #687). Its id, its links and its shares stay. `note`: what changed, in one line. The older revisions stay readable.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `artifact` | string | yes |
| `revision` | integer | yes |
| `title` | string | yes |
| `name` | string | yes |
| `type` | string | yes |
| `size` | integer | yes |
| `sha256` | string | yes |
| `by` | string | yes |
| `note` | string | no |
| `restoredFrom` | integer | no |
| `copiedFrom` | string | no |
| `mergedFrom` | string | no |
| `masked` | integer | no |
| `warning` | string | no |

```json
{
  "artifact": "a1b2c3d4-0000-4000-8000-000000000624",
  "revision": 2,
  "title": "Queue wait by hour",
  "name": "chart.html",
  "type": "text/html",
  "size": 19210,
  "sha256": "e3b0c44298fc1c149afbf4c8996fb92427ae41e4649b934ca495991b7852b855",
  "by": "job 6f1c2a9e",
  "note": "adds the hours after six"
}
```

Never the text.

## `lanes.recommended`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/lanes.recommended.v1.json`). A machine's lane recommendation changed (issue #688): the `lanes` it can run, from its resource history (`headroom`, the most lanes it ran without resource pressure or slow progress, and what each lane's cost leaves room for) and the usage it burns (`usage`: `free`, `near` the soft limit, past the `soft` limit, at the `hard` limit), within its bounds, next to the `configured` lanes the decider uses. `reason` in plain words; `confidence` 0..1 from the history it stands on. Recorded, not applied: an admin applies it. Recorded when the recommended or the configured lanes change. `mode` (`shadow`) only in one recorded while active mode was there. `decidedBy: jev`: the lanes are Jev's applied pick at the `lane-count` decision point (issue #550), and `rules` the rules' own recommendation.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `machineId` | string | yes |
| `lanes` | integer | yes |
| `configured` | integer | yes |
| `headroom` | integer | no |
| `reason` | string | yes |
| `confidence` | number | yes |
| `usage` | `free` \| `near` \| `soft` \| `hard` | yes |
| `mode` | string | no |
| `decidedBy` | string | no |
| `rules` | object | no |

```json
{
  "machineId": "laptop",
  "lanes": 4,
  "configured": 2,
  "headroom": 4,
  "confidence": 1,
  "usage": "free",
  "reason": "no resource pressure up to 2 lanes in use; a lane uses about 2.0 GiB of memory and 10% CPU: room for 2 more"
}
```

```json
  },

    "autoTune": true,
    "minLanes": 1,
    "maxLanes": 3
  },
  "by": "admin"
}
```

An admin can undo it. Without `by` (and with `configured`): the hopper applied it itself in active mode, before each one was an admin's.

```json
  "by": "admin"
}
```

## `bug_report.filed`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/bug_report.filed.v1.json`). A person filed a bug report with Report a bug (issue #694), through their own GitHub connection, on the hopper's own repository `repo`: a new issue labelled `user-report` (`kind: issue`), or a comment on a similar open one (`kind: comment`). Its `number` and `url`, the `jobId` it was about, and `by`. `fromJob`: a running job filed it about itself through the hopper (`hopper-gh report bug`), with its user's connection; `by` is then `job <id>`. `later`: a report kept while GitHub could not take it (`bug_report.kept`), sent now; `id` is its report. Never its text.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `repo` | string | yes |
| `kind` | `issue` \| `comment` | yes |
| `number` | integer | yes |
| `url` | string | yes |
| `jobId` | string | no |
| `by` | string | yes |
| `fromJob` | boolean | no |
| `id` | string | no |
| `later` | boolean | no |

```json
{
  "repo": "henningfutrell/hopper",
  "kind": "issue",
  "number": 712,
  "url": "https://github.com/henningfutrell/hopper/issues/712",
  "jobId": "b3f1c2d4",
  "by": "octocat"
}
```

## `bug_report.failed`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/bug_report.failed.v1.json`). A bug report was not filed (issue #694): GitHub refused it for good. `error` says why; `jobId`, `by` and `fromJob` as in `bug_report.filed`.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `repo` | string | yes |

| `by` | string | yes |
| `fromJob` | boolean | no |

```json
  "by": "octocat"
}
```

## `bug_report.kept`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/bug_report.kept.v1.json`). A bug report was kept to send later (issue #694): no GitHub connection, or GitHub could not take it now (no answer, no access to the repository, a rate limit, its own failure). `problem` says why; `id` is the report in Your reports. The hopper sends it later (`bug_report.filed` with `later`). `jobId`, `by` and `fromJob` as in `bug_report.filed`. Never its text.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `repo` | string | yes |
| `id` | string | yes |
| `problem` | string | yes |
| `jobId` | string | no |
| `by` | string | yes |
| `fromJob` | boolean | no |

```json
{
  "repo": "henningfutrell/hopper",
  "id": "c2a7e9d1",
  "problem": "your GitHub is not connected: connect it in Sources → Connect GitHub",
  "by": "octocat"
}
```

## `job.child_issue_filed`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/job.child_issue_filed.v1.json`). A running job filed an issue through the hopper (issue #729, issue lineage): `child`, a child of the job's own issue `parent` (each `repo` and `number`; the child's `url`). `required`: the job marked it a required child (`--required`), and the hopper linked it as a GitHub sub-issue of the parent, so the parent is not done while it is open (`subIssue`; `false` with `subIssueError` when GitHub refused the link: the issue is filed all the same). Else a follow-up: the issue's text names its parent, and nothing waits on it. `routed` (issue #1510): the hopper labelled the required child with the job sources' label and assigned it to the job's user, so Intake lists it as a request card. `unassigned` (issue #1856): the assignees GitHub did not set on it, though the hopper asked twice (GitHub drops an assignee it cannot set with no error): the issue keeps its label and waits as not assigned until a person assigns it. `requestId` names the request, as in `github_proxy.done`.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `requestId` | string | yes |
| `parent` | object | yes |
| `child` | object | yes |
| `required` | boolean | yes |
| `subIssue` | boolean | no |
| `subIssueError` | string | no |
| `routed` | boolean | no |
| `unassigned` | string[] | no |

```json
{
  "requestId": "r1",
  "parent": {
    "repo": "octo/tools",
    "number": 7
  },
  "child": {
    "repo": "octo/tools",
    "number": 42,
    "url": "https://github.com/octo/tools/issues/42"
  },
  "required": true,
  "subIssue": true
}
```

## `job.sub_issue_linked`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/job.sub_issue_linked.v1.json`). The hopper linked a job's required child as a GitHub sub-issue of its parent at a later try (issue #1607): GitHub refused the link, or did not answer, as the child was filed (`job.child_issue_filed` with `subIssue: false`). The hopper keeps such a link and tries it again until it is made. `requestId` names the request that filed the child; `parent` and `child` as there.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `requestId` | string | yes |
| `parent` | object | yes |
| `child` | object | yes |

```json
{
  "requestId": "r1",
  "parent": {
    "repo": "octo/tools",
    "number": 7
  },
  "child": {
    "repo": "octo/tools",
    "number": 42,
    "url": "https://github.com/octo/tools/issues/42"
  }
}
```

## `github_watch.changed`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/github_watch.changed.v1.json`). A GitHub watch saw its pointed job's item change (issue #427): one event per poll that found a change, with every change of that poll in `changes` — `state` (`from`, `to`: `open`, `closed` or `merged`; `reason` GitHub's state reason; `mergedAt`), `labels` (`added`, `removed`), `comments` (`added`: `id`, `author`, `at`; `removed`: how many went), `reviews` (`added`: `id`, `author`, `state`, `at`), `linkedPullRequests` (`added`, `removed`, by URL). `pointedJob`, `repo`, `pointer`: what is watched. A job on a question posted on its issue thread is watched too (issue #435): then `pointedJob` is the job's id, and the event carries `jobId`, on the job's timeline. A poll that sees no change, and the first poll of a watch, record nothing. Never a comment's text.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `pointedJob` | string | yes |
| `repo` | string | yes |
| `pointer` | object | yes |
| `changes` | object | yes |

```json
{
  "pointedJob": "p1",
  "repo": "octo-org/hello",
  "pointer": {
    "kind": "issue",
    "number": 7,
    "url": "https://github.com/octo-org/hello/issues/7"
  },
  "changes": {
    "labels": {
      "added": [
        "ready"
      ],
      "removed": []
    },
    "comments": {
      "added": [
        {
          "id": 1201,
          "author": "octocat",
          "at": "2026-10-11T12:00:00Z"
        }
      ],
      "removed": 0
    }
  }
}
```

## `infra.plan_recorded`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/infra.plan_recorded.v1.json`). A job recorded a plan of an infrastructure change (issue #870): what made it (`tool`), the asset an apply of it is minted a credential for, the workspace or app it changes (`target`), the repository, branch (`ref`) and commit it was made at, its pull request, the read profile it was made with (`read`), the job's issue, whether a saved plan file came with it (`file`), when it goes stale (`expiresAt`), and its `summary` (issue #870 part 2): what it changes in plain words, its `level` (`low` or `high`), its risk callouts (`destroy`, `iam`, `prod`, `data`, `network`), and whether it `failed` a check (a new AWS resource without the MAP tag: nobody approves such a plan). Never its text or its file. A plan is never changed once kept. The notifiers send it, with the watchers of its environments (part 4).

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `plan` | string | yes |
| `tool` | `terraform` \| `helm` \| `gitops` | yes |
| `asset` | object | yes |
| `target` | string | yes |
| `repo` | string | yes |
| `ref` | string | yes |
| `commit` | string | yes |
| `pullRequest` | integer | no |
| `read` | string | no |
| `issue` | string | no |
| `file` | boolean | yes |
| `expiresAt` | string | yes |
| `summary` | object | no |

```json
{
  "plan": "0b7e5a3c-0000-4000-8000-000000000870",
  "tool": "terraform",
  "asset": {
    "kind": "aws-role",
    "name": "123456789012/deploy"
  },
  "target": "uat-network",
  "repo": "octo-org/infra",
  "ref": "issue-12",
  "commit": "e83c5163316f89bfbde7d9ab23ca2e25604af290",
  "pullRequest": 13,
  "read": "read/aws-role/123456789012/readonly",
  "issue": "https://github.com/octo-org/infra/issues/12",
  "file": true,
  "expiresAt": "2026-10-12T11:00:00.000Z",
  "summary": {
    "words": "Adds 2 security group rules in uat; changes nothing in prod; destroys nothing",
    "level": "low",
    "risks": [
      "network"
    ],
    "failed": false
  }
}
```

## `infra.plan_approved`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/infra.plan_approved.v1.json`). A plan of an infrastructure change was approved (issue #870), on Infra: until the plan is stale, an apply that names it, made at the commit its branch is at, is minted the credential it asks. By risk (part 3): an operator or an admin approves a low-risk plan in uat only, an admin any other. `by`, who; `auto` when the hopper approved it itself, as the plan was kept, with auto-approve on; `level`, the plan's risk level, when it has a summary. On the timeline of the job that recorded the plan. The notifiers send it, with the watchers of the plan's environments (part 4).

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `plan` | string | yes |
| `tool` | `terraform` \| `helm` \| `gitops` | yes |
| `asset` | object | yes |
| `target` | string | yes |
| `by` | string | yes |
| `auto` | boolean | no |
| `level` | `low` \| `high` | no |

```json
{
  "plan": "0b7e5a3c-0000-4000-8000-000000000870",
  "tool": "terraform",
  "asset": {
    "kind": "aws-role",
    "name": "123456789012/deploy"
  },
  "target": "uat-network",
  "by": "Ada",
  "level": "low"
}
```

## `infra.out_of_band_recorded`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/infra.out_of_band_recorded.v1.json`). A read-only check — a job's, or an outside collector's with an API token (part 2) — reported an infrastructure change that did not come through IaC or GitOps (issue #871): drift (`gitops`: an app out of sync; `terraform-plan`: a non-empty plan on unchanged code) or an audit-log write (`cloudtrail`, `kube-audit`) by a principal that is no controller identity and no plan-bound apply credential. What changed (`target`), the action in the source's words (`what`), who (`who`), when (`at`), the signal's own id (`key`), and who reported it: the job whose check did and its issue, or the collector (`reporter`, its API token's label), then on no job's timeline. Never the signal's detail. On Infra until a person marks it; the notifiers send it.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `change` | string | yes |
| `source` | `gitops` \| `terraform-plan` \| `cloudtrail` \| `kube-audit` | yes |
| `key` | string | yes |
| `target` | string | yes |
| `what` | string | yes |
| `who` | string | no |
| `at` | string | yes |
| `job` | string | no |
| `issue` | string | no |
| `reporter` | string | no |

```json
{
  "change": "5d2c7a10-0000-4000-8000-000000000871",
  "source": "cloudtrail",
  "key": "6f0e8d2a-1b3c-4d5e-9f00-0a1b2c3d4e5f",
  "target": "sg-0abc1234",
  "what": "ec2:AuthorizeSecurityGroupIngress",
  "who": "arn:aws:sts::123456789012:assumed-role/Admin/console",
  "at": "2026-10-12T09:41:00Z",
  "job": "f3b1c2d4-0000-4000-8000-000000000001",
  "issue": "https://github.com/octo-org/infra/issues/20"
}
```

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `reporter` | string | yes |
| `sources` | object[] | yes |

```json
{
  "reporter": "topology collector",
  "sources": [
    {
      "key": "aws/123456789012/eu-west-1",
      "ok": true,
      "nodes": 42,
      "links": 61
    },
    {
      "key": "kubernetes/arn:aws:eks:eu-west-1:123456789012:cluster/prod",
      "ok": false,
      "error": "the API server did not answer"
    }
  ]
}
```

## `approval.confirmation_asked`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/approval.confirmation_asked.v1.json`). An API token asked to approve a high-risk infra plan or a write, sync or apply profile of a template (issue #909), and the hopper did not approve it: a person confirms it by approving the item in the UI. `kind` (`infra-plan`, `vault-profile`), `ref` the item, `words` what to approve, `asker` the API token's label. Sent at most once an hour for an item; subscribe a webhook to it to be told. On the timeline of the job that recorded the plan.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `kind` | `infra-plan` \| `vault-profile` | yes |
| `ref` | string | yes |
| `words` | string | yes |
| `asker` | string | yes |
| `plan` | string | no |
| `template` | string | no |
| `operation` | `read` \| `write` \| `sync` \| `apply` \| `observe` | no |
| `asset` | object | no |

```json
{
  "kind": "infra-plan",
  "ref": "0b7e5a3c-0000-4000-8000-000000000870",
  "plan": "0b7e5a3c-0000-4000-8000-000000000870",
  "words": "approve plan 0b7e5a3c for prod-db (high risk): Destroys 1 database in prod",
  "asker": "Grok Bot"
}
```

## `api_grant.minted`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/api_grant.minted.v1.json`). A person minted a grant for an agent (issue #881): its id, `label`, `holder`, `role`, `scopes`, whether its tokens are box tokens (`box`), its fixed end (`endsAt`, null: none) and how long its API tokens live (`tokenMinutes`). Never a token.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `grant` | string | yes |
| `label` | string | yes |
| `holder` | string | no |
| `role` | `viewer` \| `operator` \| `admin` | yes |
| `scopes` | string[] | yes |
| `box` | boolean | yes |
| `endsAt` | string \| null | yes |
| `tokenMinutes` | integer | yes |

```json
{
  "grant": "3f9a0c2e5b7d1e48",
  "label": "Grok Bot",
  "holder": "grok-bot",
  "role": "operator",
  "scopes": [
    "questions:answer",
    "sources:intake",
    "*:read"
  ],
  "box": true,
  "endsAt": "2027-01-10T09:00:00.000Z",
  "tokenMinutes": 10
}
```

## `api_grant.refreshed`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/api_grant.refreshed.v1.json`). An agent traded a grant's refresh token for a new API token and a new refresh token (issue #881): `from` is the caller, as the sign-in limit counts it. Never a token.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `grant` | string | yes |
| `from` | string | yes |

```json
{
  "grant": "3f9a0c2e5b7d1e48",
  "from": "127.0.0.1"
}
```

## `api_grant.reuse_detected`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/api_grant.reuse_detected.v1.json`). A refresh token already spent was sent again after the grace period (issue #881): it may be stolen, so the grant was revoked at once (`api_grant.revoked`, reason `reuse-detected`). `from`: who sent it. Subscribe a notifier to this to be told.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `grant` | string | yes |
| `label` | string | yes |
| `holder` | string | no |
| `from` | string | yes |

```json
{
  "grant": "3f9a0c2e5b7d1e48",
  "label": "Grok Bot",
  "holder": "grok-bot",
  "from": "203.0.113.7"
}
```

## `api_grant.revoked`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/api_grant.revoked.v1.json`). A grant ended, and every API token of it (issue #881). `reason`: `revoked` (a person revoked it), `revoked-all` (a person revoked every grant), `reuse-detected` (a spent refresh token sent again), `expired-idle` (no refresh for 30 days), `expired-absolute` (its fixed end passed), `realm-changed` (its minter's sign-in grants no role any more), or `refused` (Access refused it at its mint).

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `grant` | string | yes |
| `label` | string | yes |
| `holder` | string | no |
| `reason` | `revoked` \| `revoked-all` \| `reuse-detected` \| `expired-idle` \| `expired-absolute` \| `realm-changed` \| `refused` | yes |

```json
{
  "grant": "3f9a0c2e5b7d1e48",
  "label": "Grok Bot",
  "holder": "grok-bot",
  "reason": "reuse-detected"
}
```

## `api_tokens.settings_changed`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/api_tokens.settings_changed.v1.json`). The hopper's admin changed how long an API token lives (issue #881): `tokenMinutes`. API tokens issued after it live that long; those there are keep their own ends. In the admin's log.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `tokenMinutes` | integer | yes |

```json
{
  "tokenMinutes": 10
}
```

## `step.started`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/step.started.v1.json`). A running job's sandbox step started on its Windows host (issue #731), or in a box its own sandbox request started (issue #1004), or in a one-shot need box of a `template`, with the `needs` the vault minted its credentials for (issue #1007): `step` its id, the `host` or the `box`, its `command` (at most 300 characters), its timeout, the size of the inputs it sent and the `outputs` it asked back; `secrets`: the names of the vault secrets it was given (a Windows step; a box step, issue #1875). Never its output.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `step` | string | yes |
| `host` | string | no |
| `box` | string | no |
| `command` | string | yes |
| `timeoutSeconds` | integer | yes |
| `inputsBytes` | integer | yes |
| `outputs` | string[] | yes |
| `secrets` | string[] | no |
| `template` | string | no |
| `needs` | string[] | no |

```json
{
  "step": "5f0c1d2e-0000-4000-8000-000000000731",
  "host": "build-host",
  "command": "msbuild App.sln /p:Configuration=Release",
  "timeoutSeconds": 1800,
  "inputsBytes": 5242880,
  "outputs": [
    "src/App/bin/Release"
  ]
}
```

## `step.finished`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/step.finished.v1.json`). A sandbox step ended, on its Windows host (issue #731) or in its box (issue #1004; a need box, issue #1007): its `exit` code and how long it ran; `outputsBytes` when its outputs came back, and `outputsSha256`, their sha256 as a need box made it and the hopper checked it on arrival (issue #2288); `problem` when the hopper could not run it, stopped it (its timeout, or the job stopped waiting) or could not bring its outputs back, or its outputs held a vault secret's value and were not given (a box step, issue #1875).

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `step` | string | yes |
| `host` | string | no |
| `box` | string | no |
| `exit` | integer | yes |
| `seconds` | integer | yes |
| `outputsBytes` | integer | no |
| `outputsSha256` | string | no |
| `problem` | string | no |

```json
{
  "step": "5f0c1d2e-0000-4000-8000-000000000731",
  "host": "build-host",
  "exit": 0,
  "seconds": 94,
  "outputsBytes": 1048576
}
```

## `step.refused`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/step.refused.v1.json`). A running job asked for a sandbox step and was told no (issues #731, #1004, #1007), with `reason`: for a need step, a need the vault minted no credential for (`box`: the need box), or no container runtime; no such Windows host, no such box of the job's, a `--secret` for a box, a bad command, timeout or output, inputs too large, a secret the host does not give, or a vault secret the vault refused.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `reason` | string | yes |
| `host` | string | no |
| `box` | string | no |

```json
{
  "reason": "the hopper has no Windows host build. It has: build-host.",
  "host": "build"
}
```

## `vault.step_delivered`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/vault.step_delivered.v1.json`). A vault secret was given to a running job's Windows sandbox step (issue #731): on the step's ssh connection to the Windows `host`, into the step's environment only, never to the job, a file or an argument. Or to its box step (issue #1875): `host` the need box, the secret copied into it as a file, never into its environment or to the job. The secret's name, the host and the job; never the value. `backend`: the vault backend it was read from, when it is kept in one.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | yes |
| `host` | string | yes |
| `job` | string | yes |
| `backend` | string | no |

```json
{
  "name": "NUGET_TOKEN",
  "host": "build-host",
  "job": "f3b1c2d4-0000-4000-8000-000000000001"
}
```

## `vault.step_refused`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/vault.step_refused.v1.json`). A running job's Windows sandbox step, or its box step (`host` the need box, issue #1875), asked for a vault secret and the vault refused (issue #731): the job has no vault grant (a grant ask is opened), it is not at work, the vault holds no such secret, it is a minting credential, or it cannot be opened or read. `reason` says which; never a value.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | yes |
| `host` | string | yes |
| `job` | string | yes |
| `backend` | string | no |
| `reason` | string | yes |

```json
{
  "name": "NUGET_TOKEN",
  "host": "build-host",
  "job": "f3b1c2d4-0000-4000-8000-000000000001",
  "reason": "job f3b1c2d4 has no vault grant: a person grants it the vault on the Vault page (Settings → Vault), then ask again"
}
```

## `landing_batch.due`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/landing_batch.due.v1.json`). A batch run of a repository's landing branch is due (issue #1589): recorded before the hopper makes its `branch` at the `tip` and opens its pull request into the `tested` branch, with the text it carries (`merges`, the issues it `closes`) and `why`. A pass that stops before `landing_batch.started` starts the same batch run, and takes the pull request it finds on that branch in place of a second one.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `repo` | string | yes |
| `landing` | string | yes |
| `tested` | string | yes |
| `tip` | string | yes |
| `branch` | string | yes |
| `merges` | integer[] | yes |
| `closes` | string[] | yes |
| `why` | string | yes |

```json
{
  "repo": "owner/repo",
  "landing": "main",
  "tested": "dev",
  "tip": "0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567",
  "branch": "hopper-batch/0123456789ab",
  "merges": [
    1088,
    1090,
    1093
  ],
  "closes": [
    "#1087"
  ],
  "why": "3 merges since the last batch run"
}
```

## `landing_batch.started`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/landing_batch.started.v1.json`). The hopper started a batch run of a repository's landing branch (issue #1073, design.md "Landing batches"): `branch` made at the landing branch's `tip`, and a pull request of it (`pullRequest`, `url`) into the `tested` branch, so the full test suite runs on it. `merges`: the pull requests the batch carries, from their merge commits. `why`: the trigger (N merges, the timer, or no batch run before).

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `repo` | string | yes |
| `landing` | string | yes |
| `tested` | string | yes |
| `tip` | string | yes |
| `branch` | string | yes |
| `pullRequest` | integer | yes |
| `url` | string | yes |
| `merges` | integer[] | yes |
| `why` | string | no |

```json
{
  "repo": "owner/repo",
  "landing": "main",
  "tested": "dev",
  "tip": "0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567",
  "branch": "hopper-batch/0123456789ab",
  "pullRequest": 1101,
  "url": "https://github.com/owner/repo/pull/1101",
  "merges": [
    1088,
    1090,
    1093
  ],
  "why": "3 merges since the last batch run"
}
```

## `landing_batch.promoted`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/landing_batch.promoted.v1.json`). A batch run passed every check and the hopper merged it into the `tested` branch (issue #1073): the tested branch moved by the whole batch, to the landing branch's `tip`, in one merge commit (`merge`; absent when a person merged it first). Its branch is removed.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `repo` | string | yes |
| `tested` | string | yes |
| `tip` | string | yes |
| `pullRequest` | integer | yes |
| `url` | string | yes |
| `merge` | string | no |

```json
{
  "repo": "owner/repo",
  "tested": "dev",
  "tip": "0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567",
  "pullRequest": 1101,
  "url": "https://github.com/owner/repo/pull/1101",
  "merge": "89abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef"
}
```

## `landing_batch.failed`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/landing_batch.failed.v1.json`). A batch run did not pass (issue #1073): `reason` why — `checks` that failed, no check in time, merge conflicts with the tested branch, its branch moved, or its pull request closed without a merge. The hopper closed it and removed its branch; the tested branch did not move. `checkRuns`: the failed checks with their ids, when checks failed; then a bisect within the batch starts (`landing_batch.bisect_started`). `conflicts` true: merge conflicts with the tested branch, and a back-merge is due. Recorded before the hopper closes the pull request (issue #1589): a pass closes it while it stays open. The same `tip` does not run again: the next batch run waits for a new merge, or for the culprit's revert. `cutOff` true (issue #2086): a check was cancelled or timed out (`checks`, `checkRuns` those checks), so no bisect starts, and the same `tip` runs again, at most twice in a row.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `repo` | string | yes |
| `tested` | string | yes |
| `tip` | string | yes |
| `pullRequest` | integer | yes |
| `url` | string | yes |
| `reason` | string | yes |
| `checks` | string[] | yes |
| `checkRuns` | object[] | no |
| `conflicts` | boolean | no |
| `cutOff` | boolean | no |

```json
{
  "repo": "owner/repo",
  "tested": "dev",
  "tip": "0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567",
  "pullRequest": 1101,
  "url": "https://github.com/owner/repo/pull/1101",
  "reason": "checks failed: shard (4)",
  "checks": [
    "shard (4)"
  ]
}
```

## `landing_batch.retargeted`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/landing_batch.retargeted.v1.json`). The hopper moved a job's open pull request from the tested branch (`from`) to the landing branch (`to`) (issue #1073): a job's pull request lands on the landing branch, never on the tested branch.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `repo` | string | yes |
| `pullRequest` | integer | yes |
| `url` | string | yes |
| `from` | string | yes |
| `to` | string | yes |

```json
{
  "repo": "owner/repo",
  "pullRequest": 1090,
  "url": "https://github.com/owner/repo/pull/1090",
  "from": "dev",
  "to": "main"
}
```

## `landing_batches.changed`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/landing_batches.changed.v1.json`). An admin changed the landing batches (issue #1073): per repository (`owner/repo`, lowercased), the `landing` branch a batch run tests (issue #1142; absent in a change saved before it: `main`), the `tested` branch a green batch run moves, when a batch run starts (`everyMerges`, `everyMinutes`), and the canary window (`canaryHours`, part 5; absent: no canary step). `from` and `to` the settings, `by` who changed them.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `from` | object | yes |
| `to` | object | yes |
| `by` | string | yes |

```json
{
  "from": {
    "repos": {}
  },
  "to": {
    "repos": {
      "owner/repo": {
        "tested": "dev",
        "landing": "main",
        "everyMerges": 5,
        "everyMinutes": 60
      }
    }
  },
  "by": "owner"
}
```

## `landing_batch.bisect_started`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/landing_batch.bisect_started.v1.json`). A batch run failed its checks, so the hopper bisects within the batch (issue #1073 part 2, design.md "Landing batches"): `points` the landing branch's first-parent commits beyond the `tested` branch, oldest first, each with the pull request its merge names; the `tip` (the last point) fails with `checks`. `pullRequest`, `url`: the batch run that failed.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `repo` | string | yes |
| `tested` | string | yes |
| `tip` | string | yes |
| `pullRequest` | integer | yes |
| `url` | string | yes |
| `points` | object[] | yes |
| `checks` | object[] | yes |
| `reason` | string | yes |

```json
{
  "repo": "owner/repo",
  "tested": "dev",
  "tip": "0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567",
  "pullRequest": 1101,
  "url": "https://github.com/owner/repo/pull/1101",
  "points": [
    {
      "sha": "aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa",
      "pullRequest": 1088
    },
    {
      "sha": "fedcba9876543210fedcba9876543210fedcba98",
      "pullRequest": 1090
    },
    {
      "sha": "0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567",
      "pullRequest": 1093
    }
  ],
  "checks": [
    {
      "name": "shard (4)",
      "id": 5512
    }
  ],
  "reason": "checks failed: shard (4)"
}
```

## `landing_batch.bisect_run`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/landing_batch.bisect_run.v1.json`). A bisect run started (issue #1073): `branch` at the point `sha` (`index` in the batch), and a pull request of it into the `tested` branch (`pullRequest`, `url`), so the full test suite runs on that point. The hopper closes it when its checks end; it never merges it.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `repo` | string | yes |
| `tested` | string | yes |
| `tip` | string | yes |
| `index` | integer | yes |
| `sha` | string | yes |
| `branch` | string | yes |
| `pullRequest` | integer | yes |
| `url` | string | yes |

```json
{
  "repo": "owner/repo",
  "tested": "dev",
  "tip": "0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567",
  "index": 1,
  "sha": "fedcba9876543210fedcba9876543210fedcba98",
  "branch": "hopper-batch/bisect-fedcba987654",
  "pullRequest": 1102,
  "url": "https://github.com/owner/repo/pull/1102"
}
```

## `landing_batch.bisect_tested`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/landing_batch.bisect_tested.v1.json`). A bisect run ended (issue #1073): `outcome` `good` (every check passed), `bad` (`checks` failed), or `unknown` with its `reason` (no check in time, merge conflicts, its branch moved, closed by a person), which ends the bisect with no culprit. `cutOff` true (issue #2086): `unknown` because a check was cancelled or timed out (`checks`); the point runs again, at most twice, and only then the bisect ends. The hopper closed its pull request and removed its branch.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `repo` | string | yes |
| `tested` | string | yes |
| `tip` | string | yes |
| `index` | integer | yes |
| `sha` | string | yes |
| `pullRequest` | integer | yes |
| `url` | string | yes |
| `outcome` | `good` \| `bad` \| `unknown` | yes |
| `reason` | string | no |
| `checks` | object[] | no |
| `cutOff` | boolean | no |

```json
{
  "repo": "owner/repo",
  "tested": "dev",
  "tip": "0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567",
  "index": 1,
  "sha": "fedcba9876543210fedcba9876543210fedcba98",
  "pullRequest": 1102,
  "url": "https://github.com/owner/repo/pull/1102",
  "outcome": "bad",
  "checks": [
    {
      "name": "shard (4)",
      "id": 5530
    }
  ]
}
```

## `landing_batch.culprit`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/landing_batch.culprit.v1.json`). The bisect found the first point of the batch that fails (issue #1073): `sha`, the pull request its merge names (`pullRequest`), the `checks` that failed there, and the bisect's `results`. `batch` the batch run that failed. The hopper reverts it next and files a fix issue.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `repo` | string | yes |
| `tested` | string | yes |
| `tip` | string | yes |
| `index` | integer | yes |
| `sha` | string | yes |
| `pullRequest` | integer | no |
| `checks` | object[] | yes |
| `reason` | string | yes |
| `results` | object[] | yes |
| `batch` | integer | no |

```json
{
  "repo": "owner/repo",
  "tested": "dev",
  "tip": "0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567",
  "index": 1,
  "sha": "fedcba9876543210fedcba9876543210fedcba98",
  "pullRequest": 1090,
  "checks": [
    {
      "name": "shard (4)",
      "id": 5530
    }
  ],
  "reason": "checks failed: shard (4)",
  "results": [
    {
      "index": 1,
      "sha": "fedcba9876543210fedcba9876543210fedcba98",
      "outcome": "bad"
    },
    {
      "index": 0,
      "sha": "aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa",
      "outcome": "good"
    }
  ],
  "batch": 1101
}
```

```json
{
  "repo": "owner/repo",
  "tip": "0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567",
  "sha": "fedcba9876543210fedcba9876543210fedcba98",
  "reason": "the culprit is a direct commit, not a pull request: revert it by hand"
}
```

## `landing_batch.fix_filed`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/landing_batch.fix_filed.v1.json`). The hopper filed the fix issue for the culprit (issue #1073): `issue`, `url`, on the repository, with the hopper label and assigned to the user, so Intake takes it as any other work. Its text names the culprit, its issue, the revert, the failing checks with their output, and the bisect.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `repo` | string | yes |
| `tip` | string | yes |
| `sha` | string | yes |
| `issue` | integer | yes |
| `url` | string | yes |

```json
{
  "repo": "owner/repo",
  "tip": "0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567",
  "sha": "fedcba9876543210fedcba9876543210fedcba98",
  "issue": 1105,
  "url": "https://github.com/owner/repo/issues/1105"
}
```

## `landing_batch.pending`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/landing_batch.pending.v1.json`). The pull requests merged into a repository's landing branch that wait for a batch run (issue #1073 part 3): `merges`, beyond the `tested` branch, at the landing branch's `tip`. Recorded at a pass that starts no batch run, when they differ from the last ones recorded. The work-item ledger puts each of their items at the landing stage `waiting`.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `repo` | string | yes |
| `landing` | string | yes |
| `tested` | string | yes |
| `tip` | string | yes |
| `merges` | integer[] | yes |

```json
{
  "repo": "owner/repo",
  "landing": "main",
  "tested": "dev",
  "tip": "0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567",
  "merges": [
    1088,
    1090
  ]
}
```

## `landing_batch.back_merge_opened`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/landing_batch.back_merge_opened.v1.json`). A batch run (`batch`) had merge conflicts with the tested branch, so the hopper merged the `tested` branch into a branch at the landing branch's `tip` (issue #1073 part 4, design.md "Landing batches"): `branch`, its merge commit `merge` by GitHub's own merge, and a pull request of it into the `landing` branch (`pullRequest`, `url`). The hopper merges it once GitHub lets it.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `repo` | string | yes |
| `landing` | string | yes |
| `tested` | string | yes |
| `tip` | string | yes |
| `batch` | integer | yes |
| `branch` | string | yes |
| `merge` | string | yes |
| `pullRequest` | integer | yes |
| `url` | string | yes |

```json
{
  "repo": "owner/repo",
  "landing": "main",
  "tested": "dev",
  "tip": "0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567",
  "batch": 1101,
  "branch": "hopper-batch/back-merge-0123456789ab",
  "merge": "abcdefabcdefabcdefabcdefabcdefabcdefabcd",
  "pullRequest": 1106,
  "url": "https://github.com/owner/repo/pull/1106"
}
```

## `landing_batch.back_merged`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/landing_batch.back_merged.v1.json`). The back-merge's pull request merged into the landing branch (issue #1073 part 4): `merge` its merge commit, when known. The next batch run starts at once.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `repo` | string | yes |
| `tip` | string | yes |
| `pullRequest` | integer | yes |
| `url` | string | yes |
| `merge` | string | no |

```json
{
  "repo": "owner/repo",
  "tip": "0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567",
  "pullRequest": 1106,
  "url": "https://github.com/owner/repo/pull/1106",
  "merge": "bcdefabcdefabcdefabcdefabcdefabcdefabcde"
}
```

## `landing_batch.back_merge_failed`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/landing_batch.back_merge_failed.v1.json`). No back-merge after the batch run (`batch`) at `tip` had merge conflicts (issue #1073 part 4): `reason`, and `conflict` true when GitHub cannot merge the tested branch into the landing branch (then an issue is filed), false when there was nothing to merge or the back-merge (`pullRequest`, `url`) was closed without a merge.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `repo` | string | yes |
| `tip` | string | yes |
| `batch` | integer | no |
| `conflict` | boolean | yes |
| `reason` | string | yes |
| `pullRequest` | integer | no |
| `url` | string | no |

```json
{
  "repo": "owner/repo",
  "tip": "0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567",
  "batch": 1101,
  "conflict": true,
  "reason": "dev has changes that conflict with main at 0123456789ab: GitHub cannot merge them"
}
```

## `landing_batch.back_merge_issue_filed`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/landing_batch.back_merge_issue_filed.v1.json`). The hopper filed an issue for merge conflicts it cannot merge (issue #1073 part 4): `issue`, `url`, on the repository, with the hopper label and assigned to the user, so Intake takes it. One at a time: a later conflict files none until a back-merge or a batch run is promoted.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `repo` | string | yes |
| `tip` | string | yes |
| `issue` | integer | yes |
| `url` | string | yes |

```json
{
  "repo": "owner/repo",
  "tip": "0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567",
  "issue": 1107,
  "url": "https://github.com/owner/repo/issues/1107"
}
```

## `landing_batch.canary_started`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/landing_batch.canary_started.v1.json`). A new stable candidate is on the `canary` branch, ahead of `stable` (issue #1073 part 5, design.md "Landing batches: the canary"): `tip`, and its canary window of `hours` starts now. The installs that take stable releases early update to it first.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `repo` | string | yes |
| `canary` | string | yes |
| `stable` | string | yes |
| `tip` | string | yes |
| `hours` | integer | yes |

```json
{
  "repo": "owner/repo",
  "canary": "canary",
  "stable": "stable",
  "tip": "0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567",
  "hours": 24
}
```

## `landing_batch.canary_held`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/landing_batch.canary_held.v1.json`). Bug reports name the canary candidate within its window (issue #1073 part 5): `reports` (issues labelled `user-report`), `reason`. It does not go to `stable`; an issue is filed for it.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `repo` | string | yes |
| `canary` | string | yes |
| `stable` | string | yes |
| `tip` | string | yes |
| `reports` | integer[] | yes |
| `reason` | string | yes |

```json
{
  "repo": "owner/repo",
  "canary": "canary",
  "stable": "stable",
  "tip": "0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567",
  "reports": [
    1112
  ],
  "reason": "bug reports name it: #1112"
}
```

## `landing_batch.canary_issue_filed`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/landing_batch.canary_issue_filed.v1.json`). The hopper filed the issue for a held canary candidate (issue #1073 part 5): `issue`, `url`, with the hopper label and assigned to the user, so Intake takes it. Once per candidate.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `repo` | string | yes |
| `tip` | string | yes |
| `issue` | integer | yes |
| `url` | string | yes |

```json
{
  "repo": "owner/repo",
  "tip": "0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567",
  "issue": 1113,
  "url": "https://github.com/owner/repo/issues/1113"
}
```

## `landing_batch.canary_promoted`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/landing_batch.canary_promoted.v1.json`). The canary candidate's window passed with no bug report that names it (issue #1073 part 5): the hopper moved `stable` to its `tip` as a fast-forward, so every install on the stable channel is offered it. `why`.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `repo` | string | yes |
| `canary` | string | yes |
| `stable` | string | yes |
| `tip` | string | yes |
| `why` | string | yes |

```json
{
  "repo": "owner/repo",
  "canary": "canary",
  "stable": "stable",
  "tip": "0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567",
  "why": "no bug report named it in 24 hours"
}
```

## `landing_batch.stuck`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/landing_batch.stuck.v1.json`). The landing pass of a repository failed the same way on `passes` passes in a row since `since` (issue #1333): `error` is what failed, step by step. Recorded once per run of failures; Needs you and Settings → Landing batches show it while it lasts, and Restart batch is the way out.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `repo` | string | yes |
| `error` | string | yes |
| `since` | string | yes |
| `passes` | integer | yes |

```json
{
  "repo": "owner/repo",
  "error": "the start of a batch run: GitHub answered 422",
  "since": "2026-10-15T13:44:00.000Z",
  "passes": 3
}
```

## `landing_batch.restarted`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/landing_batch.restarted.v1.json`). A person restarted the landing batch of a repository (issue #1333, Restart batch): the batch run and the bisect run at work were closed and their branches removed (`closed`), and the next batch run starts at once at the landing branch's tip, the same `tip` too. `by` who restarted it.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `repo` | string | yes |
| `tip` | string | no |
| `by` | string | yes |
| `closed` | integer[] | yes |

```json
{
  "repo": "owner/repo",
  "tip": "0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567",
  "by": "admin",
  "closed": [
    1261
  ]
}
```

## `hopper.event_loop_stalled`

Version 1 (`docs/schemas/hopper.event_loop_stalled.v1.json`). The hopper's event loop was held for `ms` (issue #1154): for that long no request was answered and no machine's link was served. `during`: the routes of the requests in flight, never their URLs. `store`: the store calls in it (all of them, issue #1383), `ms` in all and the statements that held it longest (`what`: the verb and table, never a value). `held` (issue #1383): where the loop ran while it was held, read by a thread of its own each 5 s of it, at most three reads: `afterMs` into the stall, and the top `frames` (`function (file:line)`, the file in the hopper's tree only); absent when no read was taken. `memory`: the process's resident size and JavaScript heap in use when it ended, in MiB. `skipped`: the stalls since the last one raised, which are logged only: at most one is raised a minute. An instance event: in every user's log.

| field | type | required |
|---|---|---|
| `ms` | integer | yes |
| `during` | string[] | yes |
| `store` | object | no |
| `held` | object[] | no |
| `memory` | object | no |
| `skipped` | integer | yes |

```json
{
  "ms": 5200,
  "during": [
    "POST /job/step"
  ],
  "store": {
    "ms": 3900,
    "calls": [
      {
        "what": "SELECT jobs",
        "ms": 2100,
        "count": 3
      },
      {
        "what": "INSERT checkpoints",
        "ms": 1800,
        "count": 1
      }
    ]
  },
  "held": [
    {
      "afterMs": 5000,
      "frames": [
        "parse (src/store/db.ts:212)",
        "list (src/store/jobs.ts:88)"
      ]
    }
  ],
  "memory": {
    "rssMb": 2480,
    "heapMb": 1210
  },
  "skipped": 2
}
```
